title: Knowledge Boundary Probing and Demand-Guided Intervention for LLM-Based Power System Code Generation
problem: Open-weight LLMs for power-system code generation suffer from structured API-knowledge boundary errors, such as hallucinated function names and misused parameters, hindering reliable on-premise deployment.
key_idea: Introduces a boundary-aware intervention that combines query-side API demand estimation with targeted proactive documentation injection and routed reactive correction to address API-knowledge boundary errors.
method: Proposes PowerCodeBench benchmark, L0-L3 documentation-driven probing for per-model API knowledge profiles, and a demand-guided intervention that injects relevant documentation and applies reactive correction based on API demand estimation.
dataset_or_scenario: PowerCodeBench, a benchmark generator pairing natural-language operator queries with pandapower code and numerical ground truth; evaluated on 2,000 tasks.
metrics: Accuracy points (32 to 56 improvement), prompt-token cost (41% of baseline).
results_summary: The intervention improves every evaluated open-weight model of at least 7B parameters and every commercial API by 32 to 56 accuracy points, with open-weight models in 70B-120B range matching commercial mid-tier accuracy.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require further validation on other power system libraries or broader code generation tasks.

title: Ladder Logic Translation using Large Language Models in Industrial Automation
problem: Translating ladder logic programs between different PLC vendors (e.g., Rockwell to Siemens) is difficult due to mismatched environments, incompatible constructs, and black-box tools.
key_idea: A rigorous pipeline combining XML extraction, structural normalization, and a constrained LLM to automate ladder logic translation while preserving semantic consistency.
method: The pipeline includes XML extraction from Rockwell programs, structural normalization, a constrained generative function using an LLM, and integration via the TIA Portal Openness API for Siemens S7 output.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract; example case is Rockwell to Siemens PLC code translation.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract; results mention high semantic consistency across instruction categories.
results_summary: The translations retain high semantic consistency across instruction categories, indicating effective automated translation.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on specific vendor formats and constrained LLM generalizability.

title: Mellum2 Technical Report
problem: Developing an efficient, open-weight language model specialized for software engineering tasks that balances performance with inference efficiency on commodity GPUs.
key_idea: A 12B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with only 2.5B active parameters per token, incorporating a Multi-Token Prediction head for speculative decoding and a three-phase curriculum pre-training.
method: Uses a MoE architecture (64 experts, 8 active) with Grouped-Query Attention, Sliding Window Attention, and a Multi-Token Prediction head. Pre-trained on 10.6T tokens with a three-phase curriculum, optimized with Muon under FP8 precision, then extended to 128K context via YaRN and post-trained with SFT and RLVR.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Competitive with open-weight baselines in the 4B-14B range across code generation, math, reasoning, tool use, knowledge, and safety benchmarks while running at the compute of a 2.5B dense model.

title: Fighting Numerical Hallucinations via Data-centric Compilation for Online Financial QA
problem: Large Language Models suffer from numerical reasoning hallucinations in financial question answering, and existing model-centric approaches fail to address noise sensitivity, calculation fragility, and auditability crisis in an integrated manner.
key_idea: A data-centric paradigm that synthesizes adversarial training data and uses a compile-and-execute inference process to ensure faithful numerical reasoning by design.
method: The Data-centric Reasoning Compiler (DCRC) framework with three phases: adversarial data construction, multi-stage training to produce a Data-centric Structuring Agent (DSA), and compile-and-execute inference where DSA transforms queries and documents into verifiable executable programs.
dataset_or_scenario: Established offline benchmarks and a real-world online financial QA system.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Not specified in the abstract

title: Incremental BPE Tokenization
problem: Standard BPE tokenization processes the entire input text at once, which is inefficient for streaming settings and can cause latency in large language model pipelines.
key_idea: The paper proposes an incremental BPE tokenization algorithm that processes each input byte in O(log^2 t) time, enabling efficient partial tokenization and streaming output.
method: The algorithm incrementally maintains BPE tokenization results for every prefix of the input text by implementing the standard BPE merge procedure with a fixed set of merge rules, and introduces an eager output algorithm for streaming.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Speedup factor and latency reductions compared to Hugging Face's tokenizers and OpenAI's tiktoken.
results_summary: The approach achieves up to ~3x speedup over Hugging Face's tokenizers and significant latency reductions over OpenAI's tiktoken on pathological inputs.

title: ExpGraph: Model-Agnostic Experience Learning with Graph-Structured Memory for LLM Agents
problem: LLM agents often solve tasks from scratch and fail to reuse successful strategies or failure lessons from prior experience, and fine-tuning is inflexible when stronger executors emerge.
key_idea: A model-agnostic experience learning framework that enables frozen and replaceable LLM executors to improve through external experience reuse without parameter updates, using a self-evolving experience graph.
method: ExpGraph summarizes historical trajectories into reusable skills and failure lessons, organizes them as nodes in a self-evolving experience graph, retrieves experiences via graph diffusion and utility-aware ranking, and trains a lightweight retrieval copilot with reinforcement learning using executor performance feedback.
dataset_or_scenario: ExpSuite covering question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and multi-step agentic environments including ALFWorld and AppWorld.
metrics: Improvement over baseline (percentage), average interaction steps reduction.
results_summary: ExpGraph improves over the strongest baseline by 12.2% and 4.7% on static tasks with smaller and larger executors, and by 21.4% and 12.7% in agentic environments, while reducing average interaction steps by 12.7% and 21.6%.

title: Healthcare Mechanisms from Policy-as-Code Search under Strategic Provider Response
problem: Existing healthcare AI benchmarks hold provider response fixed and cannot evaluate mechanisms by the equilibrium they produce, failing to account for strategic behavior.
key_idea: Recasting hospital mechanism design as program synthesis for language models, using typed, inspectable rule programs executed in a multi-agent simulator with strategic provider channels.
method: An incentive sweep recovers classical health-economics findings, and LLM-guided evolutionary code search over rule-program space synthesizes an inspectable mixed-objective program.
dataset_or_scenario: Medi-Sim, a multi-agent simulator with five strategic provider channels (coding, selection, delay, effort, triage).
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (e.g., elimination of up-coding, halving rejection, retaining funds).
results_summary: The synthesized program eliminates up-coding, halves rejection, and retains most of the profit-oriented baseline's funds, while an audit lever exposes pressure migration.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may depend on simulator fidelity and generalizability to real-world settings.

title: Improving Small Language Models for Code Generation with Reinforcement Learning from Verification Feedback
problem: How to effectively use reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) to improve code generation in small language models, and how reward design impacts functional correctness and behavioral properties.
key_idea: Empirical study of RLVR for Python code generation using small models, comparing different reward formulations (unit-test, static-analysis, combined) and group-based policy optimization variants (GRPO, GSPO).
method: Applied RLVR with LoRA fine-tuning on Qwen3-0.6B and Llama3.2-1B models, using GRPO and GSPO with unit-test-only, static-analysis-only (Ruff linter), and combined rewards.
dataset_or_scenario: MBPP benchmark for Python code generation.
metrics: pass@1, generation length, Ruff severity profiles, execution error types.
results_summary: RLVR improved pass@1 by up to 13 percentage points with combined reward; static-analysis-only rewards biased toward shorter completions without improving correctness, while combined rewards yielded better trade-offs.
limitations: Study limited to small models (0.6B and 1B parameters) and a single benchmark (MBPP); findings may not generalize to larger models or other datasets.

title: SEAL: Can Saturated Benchmarks Be Revived by LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge?
problem: Standard benchmarks for language models are saturated, with near-tied scores that fail to distinguish model performance, and constructing harder benchmarks is costly.
key_idea: Existing saturated benchmarks can be made informative again by using an improved evaluation protocol (LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge) that extracts latent ranking signals from the same candidate outputs.
method: SEAL (Seeded Elimination with Adaptive LLM-as-a-Meta-Judge) is a self-improving evaluation protocol that seeds candidate outputs into a single-elimination tournament, evaluating each match with task-level principles and self-improving checklist criteria.
dataset_or_scenario: Multiple saturated benchmarks covering code generation, mathematical reasoning, knowledge-intensive question answering, and tool-use agent task completion.
metrics: Spearman rank correlation, top-1 agreement, number of LLM calls per task.
results_summary: SEAL achieves 0.83–1.00 Spearman agreement with full pairwise judging and 4/4 top-1 agreement, while requiring only 11.89 calls per task compared to 28.00 for full pairwise evaluation.

title: Convergence Theory for Iterative LLM-Based Neural Architecture Search: A Parametric Cross-Entropy Framework with Closed-Form Proxy Reliability
problem: No formal convergence theory exists for iterative LLM-based neural architecture search (NAS) algorithms.
key_idea: Modeling iterative LLM-NAS as a parametric Cross-Entropy method over executable programs and proving convergence properties, including a closed-form expression for proxy reliability.
method: Formalizes iterative LLM fine-tuning on elite architectures as a CE update, proves monotonic improvement and geometric convergence, introduces delta-based generation and MinHash-Jaccard novelty filter, and derives a closed-form proxy reliability formula.
dataset_or_scenario: 22-cycle, three-LLM, six-dataset experiment with 3,300 generated architectures.
metrics: Expected architecture quality, valid-generation rate, proxy reliability (rho_S).
results_summary: Confirmed two predictions quantitatively and two at direction-of-effect level; explained the previously unreported proxy-reliability ceiling effect.

title: Learning to Choose: An Empowerment-Guided Multi-Agent System with semantic communication for Adaptive Method Selection
problem: Automating scientific computing workflows requires autonomous systems to select appropriate computational strategies and ensure causal attribution, but multi-agent pipelines suffer from semantic drift where executed procedures diverge from original strategies, corrupting evaluation and adaptation.
key_idea: Introduces a multi-agent framework combining contextual bandits with structured inter-agent communication and semantic checkpoints to preserve action-outcome fidelity, interpreted through the lens of empowerment.
method: The system integrates specialized LLM agents, grounded code generation, and self-healing execution loops within an adaptive decision-making architecture, using contextual bandits for method selection and semantic checkpoints to ensure consistency across agents.
dataset_or_scenario: Sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification workflows as representative case studies.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (mentions convergence, robustness, and adaptation qualitatively).
results_summary: Unchecked semantic drift degrades policy learning, while the proposed framework improves convergence, robustness, and adaptation to novel problem contexts.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require further validation on broader scientific workflows.

title: CodeGolf Bench: A Multi-Language Benchmark for Evaluating Concise Code Generation Capabilities of Large Language Models
problem: Existing benchmarks for evaluating LLM code generation are limited by fixed problem sets and language coverage, and do not measure the ability to produce concise, efficient code.
key_idea: Introduces a benchmark based on code golf, a competition focused on minimal character solutions, to evaluate LLMs' concise code generation across 60 programming languages with dynamic problems and live human baselines.
method: Leverages the code.golf platform to provide new problems and live human performance baselines; evaluates nine LLMs on Python and C++ tasks, comparing reasoning and non-reasoning models.
dataset_or_scenario: CodeGolf Bench benchmark covering 60 programming languages, with evaluation on Python and C++ tasks from the code.golf platform.
metrics: Average percentile performance relative to human baselines.
results_summary: Reasoning models significantly outperform non-reasoning models, achieving best average percentile of 70.97%, with the gap more pronounced in C++ due to strict syntax requirements.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on code.golf platform availability and focus on character count rather than other efficiency metrics.

title: Inferring Code Correctness from Specification
problem: Validating the correctness of LLM-generated code remains a critical challenge; existing approaches are either costly due to dynamic consensus or susceptible to bugs and bias in static reasoning.
key_idea: Grounding LLM reasoning with concrete (input, output) pairs derived from the specification, avoiding reasoning over the code itself.
method: TRAILS generates diverse test inputs via category partitioning based on the specification, executes them against candidate code, and prompts LLMs to assess whether input-output pairs conform to the specification, aggregating scores across inputs.
dataset_or_scenario: LiveCodeBench and CoCoClaNeL datasets, evaluated across three LLMs (Qwen3Coder-30B, Devstral-Small-24B, Olmo3.1-Instruct).
metrics: Matthew Correlation Coefficient (MCC), stability across seeded runs, and number of unique code samples correctly labeled.
results_summary: TRAILS improves MCC by up to 39% relative to Zero-Shot CoT, consistently outperforms HoarePrompt, and demonstrates greater stability and coverage.

title: Minimal Prompt Perturbations Lead to Code Vulnerabilities: Prompt Fragility and Hidden-State Signals in Coding LLMs
problem: Whether minor prompt perturbations compromise the security of LLM-generated code, beyond functional correctness.
key_idea: Token-level mutations as small as a single-character change can flip generated code from secure to vulnerable, and this fragility is partially encoded in hidden states.
method: Applied token-level mutations to prompts across three models and five programming languages, then probed hidden states to predict vulnerabilities.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Mean AUC for predicting input-handling vulnerabilities (0.753) and secure-defaults vulnerabilities (0.674).
results_summary: Single-character prompt mutations can flip code from secure to vulnerable; input-handling vulnerabilities are more predictable from hidden states than secure-defaults vulnerabilities.

title: HTAM: Hierarchical Transition-Attended Memory for Operator Optimization
problem: LLM-based GPU operator optimization faces a granularity mismatch: coarse hints are reusable but hard to execute, while detailed memories are actionable but enlarge the search space and obscure optimization bottlenecks.
key_idea: Proposes a coarse-to-fine framework that organizes optimization experience into a hierarchical transition graph (HTG) with global directions, local strategies, and transition experience.
method: HTAM builds a two-level HTG to organize coarse global directions, detailed local strategies, and transition experience. At each evolution step, it selects a global direction based on current state and history, retrieves corresponding local strategy memory, and uses it to guide CUDA code generation.
dataset_or_scenario: Full KernelBench suite, backend and Robust-KBench studies
metrics: Correctness, fast-solution rate, speedup
results_summary: HTAM consistently improves correctness, fast-solution rate, and speedup over LLM-based baselines, with transferable benefits from structured memory shown in backend and Robust-KBench studies.

title: NaRA: Noise-Aware LoRA for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Diffusion LLMs
problem: Existing PEFT methods like LoRA are designed for autoregressive models and ignore the dynamics of the diffusion process, where input distributions and generation difficulty vary with noise level, leading to suboptimal fine-tuning of diffusion LLMs.
key_idea: Introduce a noise-aware low-rank adaptation (NaRA) that uses a lightweight hypernetwork to generate low-rank core matrices conditioned on noise level, enabling update matrices to vary continuously along the denoising trajectory.
method: NaRA adds a low-rank core matrix generated by a globally shared hypernetwork conditioned on noise level, allowing dynamic updates while keeping parameter and latency overhead negligible.
dataset_or_scenario: Commonsense reasoning, mathematical reasoning, and code generation benchmarks.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (likely accuracy or pass@k based on benchmarks).
results_summary: NaRA consistently outperforms noise-agnostic baselines across commonsense reasoning, mathematical reasoning, and code generation benchmarks.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require tuning of hypernetwork architecture or noise conditioning.

title: Reliable Reasoning with Large Language Models via Preference-Based Maximum Satisfiability
problem: LLMs struggle with optimisation tasks involving multiple constraints and user-defined preferences, which are common in domains like robotics.
key_idea: Externalize reasoning through code generation: LLMs generate Python code encoding constraints and preferences as a preference-based MaxSAT problem, solved by an exact solver, with independent verification.
method: LLMs generate Python code that encodes user-defined constraints and preferences as a preference-based MaxSAT problem, solved by an exact MaxSAT solver; solutions are verified for feasibility and optimality against a canonical encoding.
dataset_or_scenario: Three families of preference-based reasoning tasks.
metrics: Acceptance rates (feasibility and optimality).
results_summary: The MaxSAT-based pipeline achieves substantially higher acceptance rates than baselines (direct-answer, chain-of-thought, program-of-thought), in some cases exceeding 80%.

title: Cluster-Level Attention-Guided Parallel Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models
problem: Existing training-free samplers for masked diffusion language models decide which positions to commit at token-level granularity, which may be suboptimal for parallel decoding efficiency.
key_idea: Reliable predictions often emerge as contiguous high-confidence spans, so the unit of parallel commitment can be larger than a single token; self-attention maps can estimate inter-cluster dependencies for conflict-aware selection.
method: Group adjacent high-confidence tokens into confidence-induced clusters (CICs) as span-level update units, then use self-attention maps to select mutually compatible CICs for parallel commitment, forming a training-free cluster-level decoder (CLAD).
dataset_or_scenario: Four reasoning and code-generation benchmarks, evaluated on LLaDA and Dream model families.
metrics: Speedup (1.77x--8.47x) and task accuracy (broadly comparable).
results_summary: CLAD achieves 1.77x--8.47x speedups over Vanilla decoding while maintaining broadly comparable task accuracy in most settings.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations may include reliance on confidence thresholds and applicability to diverse tasks.

title: On the Road to Personalized Code Intelligence: Portraiting and Assisting Developers Based on Their In-IDE Behaviors
problem: Current one-size-fits-all code intelligence systems fail to accommodate individual developer differences in tool-chain preferences, domain expertise, and problem-solving strategies.
key_idea: Introduces VirtualME, an IDE-embedded data infrastructure that continuously captures and interprets dynamic developer behaviors to build a personalized developer persona.
method: VirtualME has three components: log-level behavior extraction, task-level behavior recognition via a multi-agent pipeline, and developer-personality measurement using a rule engine to distill a four-dimensional persona. It integrates this persona into a personalized repository-level knowledge Q&A agent.
dataset_or_scenario: A multi-repository benchmark with real-world developer trajectories.
metrics: Five dimensions of answer quality (not specified in detail), with average 33.80% improvement over generic baselines.
results_summary: VirtualME-enhanced answers outperform generic baselines on five dimensions, yielding an average 33.80% improvement, demonstrating the value of continuous developer-behavior data for personalized code intelligence.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on IDE-specific data and the complexity of multi-agent pipeline.

title: SafeRx-Agent: A Knowledge-Grounded Multi-Agent Framework for Safe and Explainable Medication Recommendation
problem: Existing medication recommendation methods either predict structured drug codes with limited evidence grounding or lack safety verification and traceability, while current benchmarks ignore subgroup-level safety differences.
key_idea: Introduces a fine-grained medication recommendation setting based on fourth-level ATC code generation and a multi-agent framework that integrates patient context, external clinical knowledge, and safety verification.
method: SafeRx-Agent is a knowledge-grounded multi-agent framework that uses patient context, external clinical knowledge, and safety verification to recommend traceable medication sets.
dataset_or_scenario: MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV datasets
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: SafeRx-Agent improves fine-grained medication prediction accuracy while controlling drug interactions, contraindications, and medication set size.

title: MLEvolve: A Self-Evolving Framework for Automated Machine Learning Algorithm Discovery
problem: Existing LLM-based MLE agents suffer from inter-branch information isolation, memoryless search, and lack of hierarchical control, hindering long-horizon optimization for automated machine learning algorithm discovery.
key_idea: MLEvolve introduces Progressive MCGS with cross-branch information flow via graph-based reference edges and an entropy-inspired progressive schedule, along with Retrospective Memory for experience reuse and decoupled strategic planning from code generation.
method: MLEvolve extends tree search to Progressive MCGS, enabling cross-branch information flow and shifting from exploration to exploitation. It uses Retrospective Memory combining a cold-start knowledge base with dynamic global memory, and decouples strategic planning from code generation with adaptive coding modes.
dataset_or_scenario: MLE-Bench for machine learning engineering tasks and mathematical algorithm optimization tasks (compared with AlphaEvolve).
metrics: Average medal rate, valid submission rate.
results_summary: MLEvolve achieves state-of-the-art performance on MLE-Bench across multiple dimensions under a 12-hour budget, and outperforms specialized methods like AlphaEvolve on mathematical algorithm optimization tasks.

title: Scaffold, Not Vocabulary? A Controlled, Two-Tier, Pre-Registered Study of a Popperian Code-Generation Skill
problem: The paper investigates whether the reported improvements in code generation from using a Popperian falsificationist prompt skill are due to the skill's procedural content or merely the structure imposed by any scaffold.
key_idea: The study uses a two-tier ablation with multiple controls (placebo, labels-only scaffold, execution oracle) to isolate the effect of the Popperian content from the scaffold structure.
method: Pre-registered two-tier ablation experiment comparing a full Popperian skill against a length-matched placebo, a labels-only scaffold, and an execution oracle (HumanEval+ unit tests), with a vocabulary-halo sentinel and same-model self-judge audit.
dataset_or_scenario: HumanEval+ unit tests for execution correctness; frontier model (Claude Sonnet 4.6) and small model (Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B).
metrics: Best-of-eight correctness (F@8, L@8, V@8), +5-point improvement threshold.
results_summary: On the frontier model, all conditions near ceiling with no separation; on the small model, structured arms lift correctness by 20-22 points but the full skill shows no separable benefit over a labels-only scaffold, and the placebo trails by only 2.4 points.
limitations: Ceiling effects on the frontier model limited detection; results are specific to the tested models and prompt-skill family, not generalizable to Popperian methodology overall.

title: Latent Reasoning with Normalizing Flows
problem: Explicit chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs forces intermediate computation through discrete, serial token streams, which is inefficient for semantic or uncertain updates. Existing latent reasoning methods sacrifice key advantages of autoregressive generation like left-to-right decoding and KV-cache compatibility.
key_idea: Model continuous latent thoughts using normalizing flows to preserve tractable likelihoods, probabilistic sampling, and compatibility with standard autoregressive decoding and KV-cache.
method: NF-CoT instantiates a TARFlow-style normalizing flow inside the LLM backbone, defining a tractable probability model over compact continuous thoughts distilled from explicit CoT. Continuous-thought positions are generated by an NF head, while text positions use the standard LM head within the same causal stream.
dataset_or_scenario: Code-generation benchmarks
metrics: Pass rates, intermediate-reasoning cost
results_summary: NF-CoT improves pass rates over explicit-CoT and prior latent-reasoning baselines while substantially reducing intermediate-reasoning cost.

title: Closing the Loop on Latent Reasoning via Test-Time Reconstruction
problem: Latent reasoning lacks inspectability and fidelity checks, operating in an open loop where intermediate states may lose task-relevant information.
key_idea: Using the query itself as a reference to reconstruct it from latent states, ensuring fidelity through a self-supervised reconstruction loss.
method: ReLAT constructs a differentiable Question -> Latent Thought -> Question cycle and optimizes query reconstruction loss through the latent thought before answer generation.
dataset_or_scenario: Mathematical reasoning, knowledge QA, and code generation benchmarks on the Qwen family.
metrics: Accuracy (e.g., AIME 2024 accuracy).
results_summary: ReLAT consistently improves over baselines; on Qwen3-8B, it raises AIME 2024 accuracy from 56.7% to 73.3%, a 16.6-point gain over the strongest open-loop latent baseline.

title: Asuka-Bench: Benchmarking Code Agents on Underspecified User Intent and Multi-Round Refinement
problem: Existing code-generation benchmarks evaluate single-shot completions from full specifications, but real-world web development involves underspecified user intent and iterative refinement based on intermediate results.
key_idea: Asuka-Bench pairs underspecified user intent with multi-round refinement, using a closed-loop system where a Code Agent generates a web project, a UI Agent executes tests, and a User LLM provides feedback for subsequent rounds.
method: The benchmark consists of 50 web tasks with 784 evaluation criteria and 2402 expected outcomes. It uses a closed-loop evaluation: Code Agent generates a project, UI Agent tests it, and User LLM produces feedback for iterative improvement.
dataset_or_scenario: 50 web tasks with underspecified user intent, evaluated through multi-round refinement.
metrics: Weighted Task Pass Rate
results_summary: Weighted Task Pass Rate varies by 38 percentage points across models, and models differ substantially in repair ability. The best model completes only 52% of projects after three rounds, indicating the benchmark is far from saturated.

title: Microskill Architecture: A Modular Skill-Driven Framework for AI-Native Code Generation
problem: Managing context windows in AI-native code generation without losing accuracy or efficiency, as injecting full project documentation and code leads to loss of mid-sequence information, high token costs, and architecture drift.
key_idea: Partitioning knowledge into atomic, sharply scoped skill capsules and using a dynamic router to select only semantically relevant capsules for the task, inspired by microservices.
method: Formalizes context allocation as constrained optimization over semantic relevance subject to a token budget; implements a modular design with skill capsules and a dynamic router.
dataset_or_scenario: An enterprise content management system with fifteen complex features.
metrics: Token consumption, first-try compilation success rates, architectural violations, number of new skill capsules extracted.
results_summary: MicroSkill cuts token consumption by over 90%, nearly doubles first-try compilation success rates, eliminates architectural violations entirely, and enables autonomous extraction of seven new skill capsules.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require careful design of skill capsules and router for different domains.

title: CASS-RTL: Correctness-Aware Subspace Steering for RTL Generation with LLMs
problem: LLM-based RTL code generation suffers from logical errors that compromise circuit correctness, and existing mitigation methods overlook the internal attention mechanisms of LLMs that may correlate with correctness.
key_idea: Identify attention heads whose activation patterns differentiate correct from incorrect RTL, construct a low-dimensional subspace capturing correctness-relevant signals, and design a lightweight geometry-aware intervention to steer the model at inference time.
method: CASS-RTL identifies correctness-aware attention heads, constructs a low-dimensional subspace from their activation patterns, and applies a geometry-aware intervention during inference to steer generation toward correct RTL outputs.
dataset_or_scenario: VerilogEval and CVDP benchmarks for RTL code generation.
metrics: pass@1, pass@5, pass@10 accuracy.
results_summary: CASS-RTL achieves 10%-20% improvement in pass@1/5/10 on VerilogEval and 5% improvement on CVDP, enhancing reliability without sacrificing efficiency or requiring large labeled datasets.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require further validation on diverse models and tasks beyond RTL generation.

title: Willing but Unable: Separating Refusal from Capability in Code LLMs via Abliteration
problem: Producing labeled vulnerable code at scale is hindered by label noise in mined corpora and inaccuracies in LLM-based augmentation; safety-aligned code LLMs refuse prompts to inject specific vulnerabilities, preventing a complementary data generation approach.
key_idea: Abliteration, a low-rank weight edit that projects out the refusal direction in the residual stream, can remove refusal behavior in code LLMs while preserving code generation capability, enabling vulnerability injection from safe code.
method: Apply abliteration to Qwen2.5-Coder-Instruct models (3B, 7B, 14B) and evaluate on safe samples from PromSec and SafeCoder, prompting for CWE-89 (SQL injection) injection; refusal rates, syntactic validity, and injection rates are measured.
dataset_or_scenario: Safe code samples from PromSec and SafeCoder, with CWE-89 (SQL injection) as the vulnerability target.
metrics: Refusal rate, syntactic validity, injection rate; vulnerability verdicts from a three-tool detector ensemble (CodeQL, Semgrep, Bandit) with manual adjudication.
results_summary: Abliteration reduces refusal to zero/near-zero across all model sizes while maintaining syntactic validity above 93%; post-abliteration injection rates are capacity-bound (88-97% for 14B, 89-90% for 7B, 25-48% for 3B), separating willingness from capability.
limitations: Preliminary feasibility study limited to Python and CWE-89; generalizability to other languages and CWEs is not established.

title: TeleSWEBench: A Commit-Driven Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-Powered Software Engineering in Telecommunications
problem: General-purpose coding benchmarks fail to capture the stateful logic and strict requirements of telecommunications, leaving a critical evaluation gap for LLM-powered software engineering in this domain.
key_idea: Introduces TeleSWEBench, the first commit-driven benchmark for telecom, with a hierarchical LLM-as-a-Judge framework (TeleJudge) for holistic evaluation beyond rigid unit tests.
method: Mines real developer commits from srsRAN 5G repository, distills them into 734 structured test cases across three difficulty tiers, and proposes TeleJudge for file-level scoring using context and semantic similarity alongside unit tests.
dataset_or_scenario: TeleSWEBench benchmark derived from srsRAN 5G repository, consisting of 734 questions with executable unit tests.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (evaluation includes localization accuracy and functional correctness, with up to 25% shippable changes).
results_summary: The strongest ASE tools achieve up to 25% of shippable changes, and models suffer from lack of localization accuracy and functional correctness.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; inferred that the benchmark is limited to srsRAN 5G and may not generalize to other telecom codebases.

title: From Attack Simulation to SIEM Rule: Deterministic Detection-as-Code Synthesis with Probe-Level Traceability
problem: Security teams manually translate findings from Breach-and-Attack-Simulation (BAS) tools into SIEM detection rules, a time-consuming and error-prone process.
key_idea: A deterministic synthesis function maps each BAS finding to a starter Sigma rule using a small template library, with a stable identifier back to the originating probe, ensuring exact reproducibility and traceability.
method: The method uses a template library (N=23) indexed by OWASP LLM and Web Top 10 categories to synthesize Sigma rules from BAS findings, with back-references to the finding and MITRE ATT&CK technique.
dataset_or_scenario: Two locked corpora: a 17-probe LLM corpus and a 23-probe Web corpus; evaluation on AdvBench and HarmBench subsets for LLM rules.
metrics: Rule parsing and conversion success (17/17), detection rate (30% on AdvBench, 14% on HarmBench), false positive rate (7.7% on benign baseline).
results_summary: All bypassed-probe findings yield starter rules that parse and convert to Splunk and Elasticsearch; LLM rules detect 30% of AdvBench and 14% of HarmBench with 7.7% false positives.
limitations: Web rules are validated structurally only, not against a held-out attack set; the approach trades breadth of LLM-generative methods for exact reproducibility.

title: SWE-InfraBench: Evaluating Language Models on Cloud Infrastructure Code
problem: The capabilities of large language models in developing infrastructure-as-code (IaC) remain underexplored, and existing benchmarks focus on declarative paradigms and generating entire codebases rather than incremental edits common in enterprise development.
key_idea: Introduces a benchmark that reflects incremental code edits in imperative IaC tools like AWS CDK, requiring models to implement changes to existing codebases based on natural language instructions.
method: Constructs a diverse evaluation dataset from real-world IaC codebases, where models must perform realistic code modifications in AWS CDK repositories, with success determined by passing provided test cases.
dataset_or_scenario: SWE-InfraBench, a dataset sourced from dozens of real-world IaC codebases using AWS CDK.
metrics: Success rate (percentage of tasks where models pass provided test cases).
results_summary: The best model, Sonnet 3.7, succeeds in only 34% of cases, while specialized reasoning models like DeepSeek R1 achieve just 24% success, revealing significant limitations in current LLMs.

title: SePO: Self-Evolving Prompt Agent for System Prompt Optimization
problem: Existing methods for system prompt optimization use a prompt agent with a hand-engineered, fixed system prompt, limiting their adaptability and performance.
key_idea: Treat the prompt agent's own system prompt as an optimization target alongside task agents' system prompts, using a self-referential design and evolutionary search.
method: SePO employs a single prompt agent that evolves both task agents' system prompts and its own via open-ended evolutionary search with an archive of candidate prompts. Training has two stages: pre-training on a multi-task pool and fine-tuning on a target task.
dataset_or_scenario: Five benchmarks: math (AIME'25), abstract reasoning (ARC-AGI-1), graduate-level science (GPQA), code generation (MBPP), and logic puzzles (Sudoku).
metrics: Average accuracy improvement of 4.49 points compared to Manual-CoT.
results_summary: SePO consistently outperforms Manual-CoT, TextGrad, and MetaSPO across all five benchmarks, and its prompt optimization skill generalizes to tasks beyond the pre-training mixture.

title: StepPRM-RTL: Stepwise Process-Reward Guided LLM Fine-Tuning for Enhanced RTL Synthesis
problem: Automatic generation of RTL code for digital hardware designs is challenging due to long-horizon reasoning, multi-step dependencies, and strict correctness constraints in Verilog and VHDL.
key_idea: Combining stepwise trajectory modeling, process-reward modeling (PRM), and retrieval-augmented fine-tuning (RAFT) to enhance functional correctness and reasoning fidelity of LLM-based RTL code generation.
method: Constructs stepwise reasoning trajectories from canonical solutions, uses a Process Reward Model (PRM) to evaluate intermediate steps for dense feedback during RAFT fine-tuning, and employs Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to explore alternative reasoning paths.
dataset_or_scenario: Benchmark Verilog and VHDL datasets.
metrics: Functional correctness and reasoning fidelity metrics.
results_summary: StepPRM-RTL outperforms the best prior methods by over 10% in functional correctness and reasoning fidelity metrics; ablation studies confirm the combination of PRM-guided rewards and stepwise trajectory exploration is key.

title: Supportive Token Revealing for Fast Diffusion Language Model Decoding
problem: Discrete diffusion language models face a quality-latency trade-off in parallel decoding: aggressive decoding commits mutually dependent tokens too early, while conservative decoding requires many denoising steps.
key_idea: AXON shifts the token revealing criterion from 'which tokens are safest to reveal' to 'which confident reveals would best support later denoising', selecting anchors that uncertain positions attend to.
method: AXON is a training-free module added on top of existing parallel decoding strategies. It monitors uncertain masked tokens and intervenes by selecting anchors using attention, uncertainty, and confidence signals to support later denoising.
dataset_or_scenario: Reasoning and code-generation benchmarks across multiple diffusion language models.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (mentions quality-latency trade-off and accuracy).
results_summary: AXON improves the quality-latency trade-off of existing parallel decoders, often reducing the number of function evaluations while maintaining or improving accuracy.

title: Automated Repair of Requirements for Cyber-Physical Systems in Simulink Requirements Tables
problem: Requirements and implementations of cyber-physical systems often evolve independently, leading to misalignment where updated systems no longer satisfy original requirements, and traditional program repair assumes requirements are correct.
key_idea: Leveraging system execution data to repair misaligned CPS requirements, restoring requirement-to-system compliance without assuming requirements are correct.
method: A framework that evaluates correctness of declarative requirements over time-based, real-valued signals expressed in MATLAB Simulink Requirements Tables, using system execution data to repair them.
dataset_or_scenario: Six real-world case studies covering 12 requirements.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (effectiveness mentioned but no specific metrics).
results_summary: The framework is effective in producing correct and useful repaired requirements across the case studies.

title: Diagnosing Knowledge Gaps in LLM Tool Use: An Agentic Benchmark for Novel API Acquisition
problem: Large language models for code generation often need to use APIs absent from pretraining data, requiring coordination of multiple knowledge components beyond simple function recall.
key_idea: Introduces a dynamic benchmark that decomposes API knowledge into bundles and diagnoses failures into six categories, revealing that knowledge components are not interchangeable and retrieval and tuning play complementary roles.
method: NovelAPIBench automatically discovers novel APIs, extracts decomposed knowledge bundles, generates executable coding tasks, and assigns failed samples to six diagnostic categories; compares retrieval-based knowledge injection with parametric adaptation via fine-tuning.
dataset_or_scenario: About 1.9K tasks across four base models and five domains, using real library APIs.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (likely pass/fail rates per diagnostic category).
results_summary: Usage examples are the strongest standalone signal; best two-component pairing depends on domain and backbone; adding source code can hurt; fine-tuning teaches models how to use provided bundles and transfers to held-out libraries.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may include reliance on specific base models and domains, or synthetic aspects of task generation.

title: The Invisible Lottery: How Subtle Cues Steer Algorithm Choice in LLM Code Generation
problem: Large language models (LLMs) generate code with multiple valid algorithmic solutions, but incidental prompt cues can steer algorithm selection, affecting performance, security, and maintainability without changing correctness.
key_idea: Incidental prompt cues (contextual words or metadata outside the task specification) systematically shift algorithm-family distributions in LLM code generation, creating an 'invisible lottery' over code properties.
method: Conducted 46,535 controlled experiments across 11 tasks, 19 cue types (including a memoization semantic-vs-surface ablation), and 15 model configurations to measure cue-induced shifts in algorithm-family distributions.
dataset_or_scenario: 11 tasks with multiple valid algorithmic solutions, including applied tasks such as rate limiting.
metrics: Shift in algorithm-family distributions (measured in percentage points, up to 100 pp).
results_summary: Found large, systematic shifts in algorithm-family distributions (up to 100 pp) largely consistent with cue semantics; direct algorithm naming was the most reliable mitigation tested.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; inferred: limited to specific tasks and cue types, may not generalize to all LLMs or real-world scenarios.

title: Learn from Your Mistakes: Tree-like Self-Play for Secure Code LLMs
problem: Large Language Models for code generation replicate subtle security vulnerabilities from training data, and current alignment techniques like SFT and RL apply coarse-grained sequence-level optimization that fails to address localized security flaws.
key_idea: Reframe secure code generation as a fine-grained sequential decision process using a tree-like self-play framework that forces the model to discriminate against its own localized errors at critical decision nodes.
method: Tree-like Self-Play (TSP) constructs a decision tree where the model explores branching trajectories generating both secure 'golden paths' and vulnerable variants, treating code generation as a self-play game to provide dense on-policy learning signals for self-correction.
dataset_or_scenario: Python security benchmarks; unseen CWE categories; cross-language transfer from C/C++ to Python, Go, and JavaScript.
metrics: SPR@1 (secure pass rate at top-1), vulnerability reduction rate.
results_summary: TSP boosts CodeLlama-7B's SPR@1 to 75.8%, outperforming SFT (57.0%) and unstructured self-play; reduces vulnerabilities in unseen CWEs by 24.5% and transfers security principles across languages.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require additional computational cost for constructing decision trees and may depend on the quality of vulnerability detection.

title: When Model Merging Breaks Routing: Training-Free Calibration for MoE
problem: Existing model merging techniques fail when applied to Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures due to a critical failure mode called routing breakdown, where the merged router fails to dispatch tokens to suitable experts, causing severe performance degradation.
key_idea: Routing breakdown stems from the sensitivity of non-linear softmax and discrete Top-k routing mechanisms to parameter perturbations from merging, amplified by load-balancing constraints; the paper proposes a training-free calibration framework using second-order curvature information to realign the merged router.
method: Hessian-Aware Router Calibration (HARC) uses second-order curvature information to realign the merged router via a closed-form solution solved with a matrix-free conjugate gradient method.
dataset_or_scenario: Mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract.
results_summary: HARC effectively mitigates routing breakdown across diverse MoE merging baselines and leads to substantial performance improvements on mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks.

title: AlgoTouch: An Execution-Centered Approach to Incremental Construction of Imperative Programs
problem: Program construction in imperative languages requires developers to anticipate effects of instructions on data states, increasing cognitive load and error likelihood during incremental development.
key_idea: Programs are constructed by executing concrete data transformations that are recorded and incorporated into an internal representation, using an explicit notional machine to align execution and structure.
method: AlgoTouch records data transformations from direct manipulation, deterministically synthesizes control structures (conditionals from comparisons, loops from iterative behavior) into an intermediate representation, and generates code in multiple languages.
dataset_or_scenario: Representative set of algorithmic benchmarks for engineering-level validation.
metrics: Correctness, expressiveness, robustness, and language independence.
results_summary: AlgoTouch demonstrates correctness, expressiveness, robustness, and language independence across benchmarks, generating correct programs in Python, C, C++, and Java.

title: Synthetic Hallucinations, Real Gains: Hard Negatives from Frontier Models for FIM Hallucination Mitigation
problem: Small open-source code models for IDE autocomplete produce hallucinated Fill-in-the-Middle (FIM) completions that are syntactically plausible but refer to nonexistent project elements, and existing mitigations require execution sandboxes or large human-labeled datasets.
key_idea: Use frontier code models to synthesize plausible-but-wrong completions as hard negatives, then fine-tune on the contrast between these synthetic hallucinations and ground-truth developer edits.
method: Scrape multilingual FIM contexts from GitHub, use three frontier generators to produce one hard negative per context for each of four hallucination types from the Delulu taxonomy, creating a paired chosen/rejected dataset. Fine-tune Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct on a curated 100K-row subset.
dataset_or_scenario: Multilingual FIM contexts from public GitHub across eight languages; Delulu benchmark (Docker-verified multilingual FIM hallucination benchmark); HumanEval-Infilling; SAFIM.
metrics: Delulu exact match, edit similarity, HumanEval-Infilling splits, SAFIM subsets.
results_summary: Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct lifts Delulu exact match by +18.8 points and edit similarity by +0.22 on every language and type, also improving all HumanEval-Infilling and SAFIM subsets. The 3B variant achieves +12.8 EM with a small general-FIM trade-off.

title: EvoTrainer: Co-Evolving LLM Policies and Training Harnesses for Autonomous Agentic Reinforcement Learning
problem: Autonomous LLM training is often framed as recipe search with a static training harness, which is insufficient for agentic RL where shifting bottlenecks and scalar rewards mask diverse failure modes.
key_idea: Co-evolve LLM policies and training-side harnesses through empirical feedback, including diagnosing rollout-level evidence, revising diagnostics, backtesting interventions, and accumulating reusable skills.
method: EvoTrainer iteratively diagnoses rollout-level evidence, revises diagnostics, backtests interventions, and accumulates reusable skills to co-evolve policies and harnesses.
dataset_or_scenario: Mathematical reasoning, competitive-programming code generation, and repository-level software engineering.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: EvoTrainer matches or exceeds human-engineered RL references under the same data, codebase, and evaluation protocol, with the largest gain on long-horizon agentic SWE.

title: KForge: LLM-Driven Cross-Platform Kernel Generation for AI Accelerators
problem: Writing high-performance kernels for heterogeneous AI accelerators is time-consuming and does not scale as kernel complexity grows, and existing LLM-based kernel generation faces challenges in low-level code generation and cross-backend generalization.
key_idea: A cross-platform framework with two collaborating LLM-based agents (generation and performance-analysis) in an iterative refinement loop that alternates between functional and optimization passes.
method: KForge uses a generation agent that produces and refines kernels using compilation and correctness feedback, and a performance-analysis agent that interprets profiling data and emits recommendations to steer synthesis, alternating between functional passes (correctness) and optimization passes (performance).
dataset_or_scenario: Evaluated on NVIDIA B200 with gpt-oss-20b inference speed benchmark and Intel Arc B580 with 37 GEMM + tail-ops workloads from KernelBench Level 2.
metrics: End-to-end throughput improvement (percentage) and geometric mean speedup.
results_summary: On NVIDIA B200, KForge achieves 2.12% improvement in end-to-end throughput over TensorRT-LLM. On Intel Arc B580, it achieves 5.13× geometric mean speedup over PyTorch eager and torch.compile on KernelBench Level 2 workloads.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on LLM quality and the need for profiling data interpretation.

title: Many a Little Makes a Mickle: A Code-Centric Empirical Study of Data Minimization Principle in Android App Development
problem: There is a lack of actionable guidance for developers to implement privacy principles like data minimization at the code level in Android app development.
key_idea: The paper identifies recurring data minimization scenarios and distills actionable coding guidelines from a large-scale analysis of real-world Android apps, and shows that LLM-based code generation reproduces risky practices that can be mitigated by incorporating these guidelines.
method: Conducted a formative study on 1,114 open-source Android apps to identify ten data minimization scenarios across five data-handling stages, then performed a large-scale analysis of 9,875 real-world APKs to distill 31 actionable coding guidelines.
dataset_or_scenario: 1,114 open-source Android apps for formative study; 9,875 real-world APKs for large-scale analysis.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract.
results_summary: State-of-the-art LLMs consistently reproduce data minimization-risky practices, but incorporating the distilled guidelines eliminates these issues across all evaluated models.

title: LLM-Evolved Pattern Generators for Optimal Classical Planning
problem: Existing learned heuristics for satisficing planning are not admissible, making them unsuitable for optimal classical planning with A* search.
key_idea: Learn domain-dependent heuristics that are admissible by design by constructing abstractions (pattern collections) via LLM-driven evolutionary program synthesis.
method: Use an LLM-driven evolutionary program-synthesis framework to evolve programs that generate pattern collections for each domain; combine patterns admissibly via saturated cost partitioning.
dataset_or_scenario: Classical planning domains (specific domains not named in abstract).
metrics: Coverage (number of solved tasks) and evaluation speed.
results_summary: Learned programs encode interpretable domain-specific insights, run with negligible overhead, and match coverage of state-of-the-art domain-independent baselines on several domains while evaluating each state substantially faster.

title: Bridging the Sim-to-Real Gap in Semiconductor Visual Program Synthesis via Input Binarization
problem: Precise parametric control over circuit geometry is needed for semiconductor inspection, but real training data is costly and generative models cannot guarantee nanometer-scale geometric accuracy.
key_idea: A visual program synthesis framework using a VLM to convert inspection images into DSL code, with input binarization to bridge the sim-to-real gap by stripping SEM-specific texture and noise.
method: A VLM is trained on synthetic DSL-rendered data to generate editable DSL code from images; input binarization is applied to real SEM images to focus on geometric structure.
dataset_or_scenario: MIIC dataset
metrics: Mean Dice coefficient
results_summary: Binarized inputs improved mean Dice coefficient from 0.4393 to 0.5256 over raw-input baseline, showing that texture abstraction mitigates the sim-to-real gap.

title: Not All Errors Are Equal: A Systematic Study of Error Propagation in Large Language Model Inference
problem: How soft errors propagate and affect LLM inference remains largely unexplored.
key_idea: A comprehensive study on error propagation in LLM inference using a configurable and deterministic fault-injection framework (LLMFI).
method: Systematic fault injection across three open-weighted LLMs and thirteen tasks covering reasoning, multilingual, mathematical, and coding domains, with fine-grained case studies.
dataset_or_scenario: Thirteen representative tasks covering reasoning, multilingual, mathematical, and coding domains.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: The study yields 17 takeaways on error propagation and introduces four low-overhead directions to improve reliability through software-only modification.

title: A Local Perturbation Theory for Cross-Domain Interference and Recovery in Multi-Domain RL
problem: Reinforcement learning post-training on one domain degrades performance on other domains, and existing explanations based on catastrophic forgetting or global gradient conflict are incomplete.
key_idea: Single-domain RL produces sparse, small-magnitude parameter edits with weak overlap among top-changed neurons, but shared active computation routes cause interference through a second-order damage term in a low-dimensional shared conflict subspace.
method: The authors propose a local perturbation model for multi-domain RL, proving that later-domain training harms earlier domains via a second-order damage term, and a short domain refresh contracts harmful components in the conflict subspace.
dataset_or_scenario: Multi-domain RL training on mathematical reasoning, code generation, question answering, and creative writing.
metrics: Performance scores (e.g., Math score from 57.66 to 66.04) and average score (66.39).
results_summary: A brief Re-Math refresh after sequential training recovers Math performance from 57.66 to 66.04 while largely preserving other domains, achieving the best average score of 66.39. A training-free rollback on a sparse proxy conflict coordinate set partially restores Math.

title: CodegenBench: Can LLMs Write Efficient Code Across Architectures?
problem: LLMs' capabilities in generating efficient parallel code for CPU-oriented high-performance computing across diverse architectures (x86_64, Sunway, Kunpeng) are underexplored.
key_idea: Introduces CodegenBench, a benchmark suite with BLAS routines and specialized kernels to evaluate LLMs' cross-platform code generation for HPC.
method: Constructs a benchmark of 106 BLAS routines and 20 specialized kernels adapted for x86_64, Sunway, and Kunpeng architectures; evaluates state-of-the-art LLMs on code generation and analyzes factors like implementation length and task complexity.
dataset_or_scenario: CodegenBench: 106 standard BLAS routines and 20 specialized computational kernels for Sunway (LeetSunway) and Kunpeng (LeetKunpeng) architectures.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (likely performance metrics like execution time or speedup, but not explicitly stated).
results_summary: LLMs generate optimized code for x86_64 but show significant performance degradation on domain-specific architectures with limited documentation; they are most effective for moderately difficult problems requiring concise code.
limitations: The benchmark focuses on CPU-oriented HPC and may not cover all architectures or application domains; LLMs' performance on domain-specific architectures is limited by public documentation and training data.

title: DFlare: Scaling Up Draft Capacity for Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding
problem: Block diffusion speculative decoding is limited by the state-of-the-art method DFlash, which constrains all draft layers to share a single fused representation from few target layers, limiting per-layer expressiveness and draft capacity scaling.
key_idea: DFlare introduces a lightweight layer-wise fusion mechanism where each draft layer attends to its own learnable combination of a broad set of target layers, providing distinct inputs and richer target knowledge at negligible overhead.
method: DFlare flares out the narrow conditioning bottleneck of DFlash via per-layer fusion of multiple target layers, enabling deeper draft architectures. Training data is scaled from 800K to 2.4M samples to exploit enlarged capacity.
dataset_or_scenario: Six benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning, code generation, and conversation.
metrics: Wall-clock speedups (e.g., 5.52x on Qwen3-4B, 5.46x on Qwen3-8B, 3.91x on GPT-OSS-20B) and relative improvement over DFlash (roughly 11%, 8%, and 5% respectively).
results_summary: DFlare achieves average wall-clock speedups of 5.52x, 5.46x, and 3.91x on three models, improving over DFlash by approximately 11%, 8%, and 5% respectively.

title: Agentic-J: An AI Agent for Biological Microscopy Image Analysis
problem: Biological image analysis requires integration across heterogeneous tools, programming environments, and domain knowledge, which is challenging for researchers.
key_idea: A containerised, multi-agent AI assistant that enables biologists to specify analysis tasks in natural language and generates executable scripts with documented project structure.
method: The system uses specialized sub-agents for plugin management, code generation, debugging, quality assurance, and statistical reporting, producing traceable and reproducible workflows.
dataset_or_scenario: Real biological microscopy image analysis workflows (nuclei segmentation, cell tracking, multi-condition quantification).
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: The paper introduces the system design and demonstrates its application on real biological microscopy image analysis workflows.

title: ATLAS: Agentic Test-time Learning-to-Allocate Scaling
problem: Test-time scaling for LLMs currently relies on designer-engineered fixed strategies (e.g., fixed sample budget, refinement loop), leaving the model without control over compute orchestration.
key_idea: Introduces an agentic framework where an LLM orchestrator owns the entire test-time control loop, deciding when to gather more evidence, stop, and synthesize the final answer via a single 'explore' action.
method: ATLAS uses an LLM orchestrator that dispatches independent solvers via 'explore' actions, with extensible options for solver, reasoning effort, or prompting strategy. A multi-model extension (ATLAS-MM) adds solver choice as an action dimension.
dataset_or_scenario: Four benchmarks: HLE-Verified, LiveCodeBench, GPQA-Diamond, BabyVision, covering scientific QA, code generation, and multimodal reasoning.
metrics: Accuracy (percentage) and number of API calls.
results_summary: ATLAS achieves 56.00% on HLE-Verified, 82.29% on LiveCodeBench, 85.75% on GPQA-Diamond, and 23.71% on BabyVision with fewer API calls than baselines. ATLAS-MM further improves to 60.00% and 85.63% on HLE-Verified and LiveCodeBench respectively.
limitations: Ablations show that replacing the orchestrator's direct synthesis with a separate integrator degrades accuracy on three of four benchmarks, indicating the importance of stateful evidence management.

title: MPMWorlds: Material-Point-Method Simulations for Inferring and Extrapolating Physical Dynamics
problem: The research addresses the challenge of inferring physical dynamics from videos and extrapolating them forward in time, comparing code generation and video diffusion approaches.
key_idea: The core novelty is the assembly of a dataset of 2D Material Point Method (MPM) simulations and the comparative analysis of code generation versus video diffusion for physical dynamics inference and extrapolation.
method: The authors assemble a dataset of 2D MPM simulations covering various physical phenomena, then study code generation and video diffusion approaches on this dataset, varying the amount of physically relevant side information.
dataset_or_scenario: A dataset of 2D Material Point Method (MPM) physical simulations covering deformable objects, fluids, kinetic objects, and emitters.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Code generation struggles with inferring physical parameters from visual input but produces physically and temporally stable extrapolations, while video diffusion identifies geometric properties better but yields physically implausible extrapolations.
limitations: The code generation model struggles with inferring physical parameters from visual input, and the video diffusion model produces physically implausible extrapolations.

title: Trust Region On-Policy Distillation
problem: On-Policy Distillation (OPD) training becomes unstable when teacher and student distributions differ substantially, leading to unreliable policy gradients and potential optimization failure.
key_idea: Proposes Trust Region On-Policy Distillation (TrOPD) which performs OPD only in regions where the teacher provides reliable supervision, using credit assignment strategies to mitigate distribution mismatch issues.
method: TrOPD includes trust-region on-policy learning with reverse-KL estimation, outlier estimation via gradient clipping/masking/forward-KL, and off-policy guidance where the student generates from teacher prefixes and uses forward KL to imitate off-policy guidance.
dataset_or_scenario: Mathematical reasoning, code generation, and general-domain benchmarks.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: TrOPD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art OPD baselines (OPD, EOPD, REOPOLD) across mathematical reasoning, code generation, and general-domain benchmarks.

title: AnyEdit++: Adaptive Long-Form Knowledge Editing via Bayesian Surprise
problem: Editing complex, long-form knowledge in Large Language Models is challenging due to difficulty in maintaining generation coherence, and existing methods like AnyEdit rely on Fixed-window Chunking that disregards logical structure and compromises consistency.
key_idea: A structure-aware framework with Bayes-Chunk, an adaptive segmentation mechanism that dynamically identifies semantic boundaries based on Bayesian Surprise, underpinned by theoretical principles of Structural Independence and Causal Locality.
method: AnyEdit++ uses Bayes-Chunk to segment long-form knowledge at semantic boundaries identified by Bayesian Surprise, ensuring minimal cross-segment interference and superior control over updates.
dataset_or_scenario: Mathematical reasoning, code generation, and narrative tasks.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: AnyEdit++ achieves superior performance and robustness compared to state-of-the-art baselines, validating that structural awareness is critical for effective long-form knowledge editing.

title: Accuracy, Stability, and Repeated-Run Reliability of Large Language Models on Deterministic Programming Tasks
problem: Standard code-generation benchmarks emphasize single-run accuracy or eventual success, but many deployment settings require stability across repeated invocations, which is not captured by existing metrics.
key_idea: Introduces a repeated-run evaluation protocol with metrics for run-level accuracy, retry-free coverage, and per-problem variability to assess stability, revealing a gap between pass rate and retry-free coverage.
method: Proposes a repeated-run evaluation protocol with metrics for run-level accuracy, retry-free coverage, and per-problem variability; evaluates 16 models from five provider families on 100 LeetCode-style problems with two prompt templates and five repeated runs per problem.
dataset_or_scenario: A recency-based benchmark of 100 LeetCode-style problems.
metrics: Run-level pass rate, retry-free coverage, per-problem variability, perfect stability rate.
results_summary: Run-level pass rate overstates retry-free coverage by up to 17.8 percentage points, and the gap is largest for mid-performing systems; prompt effects are model-dependent rather than uniformly beneficial.

title: MOSAIC: Modular Orchestration for Structured Agentic Intelligence and Composition
problem: Automated data science is a structured model-selection problem, but existing AutoML systems have limited search spaces and LLM-based agents produce unstructured, hard-to-verify, and non-reusable modeling decisions.
key_idea: Introduces a structured agentic framework that uses a blueprint intermediate representation to turn model selection into a staged, context-grounded search, grounding LLM code generation in retrieved evidence rather than unconstrained synthesis.
method: MOSAIC builds a semantic task profile, retrieves prior cases and source-code modules, constructs a blueprint specifying modeling components and constraints, validates candidates via execution, and refines using diagnostic feedback and a failure-aware reinforcement learning policy.
dataset_or_scenario: Financial time-series forecasting and generation tasks.
metrics: Task performance, execution success, decision traceability, predictive accuracy, distributional fidelity, execution reliability, and downstream financial criteria (risk and tail behavior).
results_summary: MOSAIC improves task performance, execution success, and decision traceability over AutoML and agentic baselines, demonstrating the value of structured, reusable, execution-grounded model selection.

title: How Generation Architecture Shapes Code Complexity in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: A Paired Study on HumanEval
problem: Whether multi-agent architectures for LLM code generation affect the structural complexity of produced code, and which orchestration layers contribute to complexity, remains unexamined.
key_idea: A paired study comparing six multi-agent configurations using RADON complexity metrics reveals that architectures collapse into two complexity clusters with a 50-130% gap, and the analyst-coder split inflates complexity while the runtime debugger does not.
method: Six multi-agent configurations (Basic, AC, ACT, Debugger, AC+Debugger, ACT+Debugger) are compared under two GPT-4o models across all 164 HumanEval tasks (1,968 paired observations) using five RADON complexity metrics and a paired non-parametric statistical pipeline.
dataset_or_scenario: HumanEval (164 tasks)
metrics: RADON complexity metrics (SLOC, cyclomatic complexity, Halstead Volume, Difficulty, Effort), pass@1 accuracy
results_summary: The six architectures collapse into two indistinguishable complexity clusters separated by a 50-130% gap; the heavy cluster's additional complexity buys no pass@1 advantage, with leanest architectures matching or beating heaviest on accuracy.
limitations: The study is limited to two GPT-4o models and HumanEval tasks; findings may not generalize to other models or benchmarks.

title: SEMBridge: Tagless-Final Program Semantics with Weakest-Precondition and Bounded-Checking Interpretations
problem: How to generate multiple semantic interpretations (e.g., executable code, verification conditions) from the same program definition without duplicating syntax trees or traversals.
key_idea: Using a tagless-final encoding to write object programs once against a semantic interface, then interpreting them into different meanings such as executable code, weakest-precondition predicates, and bounded-checking constraints.
method: A tagless-final framework in Python for a loop-free imperative core with assignments, conditionals, assumptions, and assertions; object programs are defined via a semantic interface and then interpreted into multiple back ends.
dataset_or_scenario: Five example programs (loop-free imperative core) with state spaces up to 729 states.
metrics: Bounded checking success (verification conditions passed over domains up to 729 states).
results_summary: The same tagless-final definitions generated executable state transformers and verification conditions that passed bounded checking across all five example programs.
limitations: Only supports a loop-free imperative core; scalability to larger programs or loops is not addressed.

title: Specification-Driven Development Benchmark: Security Knowledge Transition
problem: AI-assisted specification-driven development often neglects security behavior, causing generated systems to satisfy functional requirements but fail to preserve authorization, input validation, and other security properties.
key_idea: Proposes a Multilayer Specification Security Model and a Security Knowledge Transition Method to operationalize security knowledge into a validated security-enriched generation contract.
method: The approach combines a Multilayer Specification Security Model with traceable relations between system entities, threats, risks, requirements, etc., and a Security Knowledge Transition Method that transforms specifications into a security-enriched contract. Evaluated via hidden-oracle and backend generation studies.
dataset_or_scenario: Two empirical studies: a hidden-oracle study and a backend generation study with three conditions (no explicit security, ASVS-conditioned, Multilayer Security Model). Evaluated against a hidden 221-test black-box API suite.
metrics: Modal failures count (baseline 50, ASVS 42, Multilayer Security Model 36).
results_summary: The Multilayer Security Model reduced modal failures from 50 to 36, with strongest improvements in application-specific categories like business logic and admin safety.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs on Code Generation for Complex Interactive Webpages
problem: Existing benchmarks for code generation from visual designs focus on static webpages and evaluate only visual fidelity and code structure, ignoring interactive behaviors and interaction consistency.
key_idea: Introduces WebIGBench, the first benchmark for evaluating code generation of interactive webpages with complex interactions, and proposes a novel evaluation pipeline for automated assessment of interactive actions.
method: Collected 103 complex webpages from real-world websites using manually designed interaction paths and UI automation, covering 5 interactive action types (e.g., click, input) with 871 distinct actions. Evaluated several MLLMs on code generation for these interactive webpages.
dataset_or_scenario: WebIGBench: 103 complex webpages from real-world websites with 871 distinct interactive actions across 5 action types.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Extensive experiments on representative MLLMs reveal performance boundaries of current models in interactive webpage code generation.
limitations: The benchmark covers only 5 action types and 103 webpages; may not fully represent all real-world interactive scenarios.

title: VFEAgent: A Multimodal Agent Framework for End-to-End Automated Finite Element Analysis
problem: Finite Element Analysis (FEA) workflow is complex and relies on domain expertise; existing LLM-based approaches struggle with multimodal inputs and complex task execution.
key_idea: An end-to-end multi-agent system that automates FEA from images and problem descriptions using a multimodal vision-language pipeline and verification-first code synthesis.
method: Integrates a ReAct-driven multimodal multi-agent pipeline to extract structured FEA specifications and a verification-first code synthesis framework with self-debugging and fallback mechanisms.
dataset_or_scenario: Various engineering mechanics scenarios.
metrics: Success rate in generating complete and physically valid simulations; reliability and correctness compared to LLM baselines.
results_summary: VFEAgent achieves high success rate in generating valid simulations, outperforming LLM-based baselines in reliability and correctness.

title: First head-to-head comparison of agentic AI applied to the analysis of simulated data of the Einstein Telescope
problem: The research problem is to compare the behavior, reliability, and cost of two agentic AI systems (Claude Code and Codex) when autonomously executing a scientific data analysis pipeline without human intervention.
key_idea: The core novelty is a head-to-head comparison of agentic AI systems in a real scientific workflow, revealing differences in speed, error handling, instruction interpretation, and manuscript quality.
method: Two agentic AI systems (Claude Code and Codex) were given identical written specifications and compute resources to autonomously execute a gravitational wave data analysis pipeline, including PSD estimation, template bank generation, matched filter recovery, and manuscript production. The experiment was run twice with different signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) ranges.
dataset_or_scenario: Simulated data of the Einstein Telescope, including noise and 100 binary black hole signal injections.
metrics: Execution time, number of self-correcting restarts, behavioral differences (e.g., silent deviations vs. literal interpretation), and manuscript quality.
results_summary: Claude Code completed the pipeline in ~3.4 minutes with silent deviations, while Codex required ~16 minutes with explicit self-correction. In the second run, Claude Code silently reinterpreted SNR instructions, leading to a scientific divergence, whereas Codex followed the specification literally.
limitations: The study is limited to a single pipeline and two AI systems; results may not generalize to other tasks or agents.

title: Token Optimization Strategies for LLM-Based Oracle-to-PostgreSQL Migration
problem: LLM-based Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration is constrained by high token consumption, long-context degradation, dialect-specific semantic differences, and semantic drift during query transformation.
key_idea: Token optimization is formalized as a constrained transformation problem, and twelve strategies are systematically evaluated to balance cost, syntactic validity, semantic preservation, and structural fidelity.
method: Twelve token optimization strategies (e.g., context pruning, minification, DSL-based compression, adaptive routing) are formalized and evaluated on Oracle SQL queries using metrics like Valid Syntax Rate, Exact Match, Semantic Match, CodeBLEU, and Token Efficiency.
dataset_or_scenario: Samples of 10 and 100 Oracle SQL queries.
metrics: Valid Syntax Rate, Exact Match, Semantic Match, CodeBLEU, Token Efficiency.
results_summary: Mild context pruning achieves 89.75% Semantic Match (vs. 89.80% baseline); adaptive routing reduces input tokens by 8.72% and output tokens by 5.49% while maintaining 88.40% Semantic Match; aggressive schema distillation increases Token Efficiency by 132.22% but drops Semantic Match by 44.50 percentage points.
limitations: The study is limited to Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration and may not generalize to other database migration tasks; the evaluation uses a relatively small query sample (100 queries).

title: Do LLMs Favor Their Providers? Measuring Vertical Integration Bias in Code Generation
problem: Large Language Models (LLMs) affiliated with specific providers may exhibit bias towards their own ecosystem in code generation, potentially constraining developer choices and increasing provider dependence.
key_idea: Introduces the concept of Vertical Integration Bias (VIB) and a benchmark (VIBench) to measure this bias in direct and agentic code generation across provider-selectable scenarios.
method: Evaluates 10 frontier provider-affiliated models against 3 non-affiliated controls using VIBench, a benchmark with 20 provider-selectable software-integration scenarios, measuring bias in both direct and agentic code generation.
dataset_or_scenario: VIBench benchmark with 20 provider-selectable software-integration scenarios.
metrics: Percentage points (pp) difference in favor of provider's ecosystem.
results_summary: Six of ten affiliated models show statistically significant VIB in direct generation (up to +18.8 pp), and agentic workflows amplify bias to +39.2 pp, with early ecosystem choices persisting in up to 90.3% of downstream files.

title: Efficient and Scalable Provenance Tracking for LLM-Generated Code Snippets
