problem: Classical fingerprint-based plagiarism detectors are impractical for billion-scale corpora used to train modern code LLMs due to linear-time search, and there is a need for scalable provenance tracking to address legal and ethical concerns.
key_idea: A hybrid two-stage pipeline that first narrows candidate snippets via vector search and then re-ranks using exact fingerprinting, achieving logarithmic-time complexity while maintaining high precision.
method: Introduces SOURCETRACKER, a 300M-parameter encoder for code retrieval, and HYBRIDSOURCETRACKER (HST) pipeline: vector search for candidate selection followed by Winnowing fingerprint re-ranking.
dataset_or_scenario: 10M-snippet subset of THESTACKV2 dataset with verbatim and adapted snippets (identifier renaming); in vitro 100k-snippet search space.
metrics: Mean reciprocal rank (MRR) and query complexity.
results_summary: Hybrid approach achieves MRR on par with Winnowing for 30-token fragments and outperforms by up to 5.4% for windows >= 60 tokens, with logarithmic-time complexity.

title: Functional Entropy: Predicting Functional Correctness in LLM-Generated Code with Uncertainty Quantification
problem: Large language models often generate functionally incorrect code, and uncertainty quantification methods for detecting hallucinations in natural language have not been effectively transferred to code generation.
key_idea: Introduces functional equivalence methods, including functional entropy, which replace natural language inference-based semantic equivalence with an LLM-based functional equivalence assessment to better predict functional correctness.
method: Systematically evaluates token-probability-based and sampling-based UQ methods on code generation, and proposes functional equivalence methods that use LLM-based functional equivalence assessment instead of NLI.
dataset_or_scenario: Over 1,700 problems across three programming languages and five LLMs.
metrics: AUROC and calibration metrics.
results_summary: Functional equivalence methods achieve top AUROC in 11 out of 15 model-benchmark combinations and the best calibration across most settings, outperforming NLI-based counterparts and other methods.

title: Rethinking Software Empirical Studies with Structural Causal Models
problem: Traditional statistical association methods in empirical software engineering (ESE) are limited in mitigating confounding bias, leading to potential false positives when evaluating causal relationships.
key_idea: Introduces CausalSE, a framework that operationalizes Judea Pearl's causal inference paradigm using Structural Causal Models (SCMs) to rigorously identify and quantify causal relationships in software experiments.
method: CausalSE applies SCMs and propensity score matching to control for confounding bias; demonstrated via a case study on prompt engineering strategies for code generation with GPT-3 using the Galeras dataset.
dataset_or_scenario: Galeras dataset; case study on prompt engineering strategies for code generation with GPT-3.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (associational vs. causal effect estimates).
results_summary: Associational analyses suggested improvements from more complex prompts, but causal analysis found no significant treatment effect, highlighting false positive risks when confounding is unaddressed.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; inferred: the framework's effectiveness may depend on correct specification of causal graphs and availability of appropriate data for matching.

title: Efficient Post-training of LLMs for Code Generation With Offline Reinforcement Learning
problem: Online reinforcement learning for code generation is resource-intensive due to LLM inference and output verification, and the paper explores whether offline RL can be an effective alternative.
key_idea: Offline reinforcement learning can be effectively applied to post-train code-generating LLMs by leveraging existing code datasets, avoiding the computational cost of online RL.
method: The paper applies offline RL to code-generating models using existing code datasets as training data, without requiring online interaction or verification.
dataset_or_scenario: Existing code datasets (not specified in detail) are used for offline RL training.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract.
results_summary: Offline RL is shown to be an effective training strategy for improving LLM performance, particularly beneficial for small LLMs and challenging coding problems.
limitations: The abstract does not specify limitations, but offline RL may be limited by the quality and coverage of existing datasets.

title: From paper to benchmark: agentic, framework-based reproduction of under-specified methods in machine health intelligence
problem: Reproducing under-specified methods in Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) is difficult due to restricted data access, incomplete reporting, and implicit design choices, leading to non-comparable implementations.
key_idea: Introducing an agentic, framework-based approach that uses a slot-binding interface to map paper descriptions into structured components of a shared PHM benchmark framework, enabling consistent and comparable benchmarking.
method: An agent translates a paper into a shared PHM benchmark framework via a slot-binding interface that maps equations and protocols into structured components (task definitions, dataset adapters, windowing, targets, models, evaluators), explicitly recording unresolved assumptions.
dataset_or_scenario: 16 PHM papers
metrics: Reproduction success, model-based code evaluation, framework binding of paper assumptions, cross-paper benchmark comparability under standardized protocols.
results_summary: Coupling agentic generation with a shared framework transforms paper reproduction into executable, assumption-aware, and systematically comparable benchmark implementations.

title: Empirical Study on the Characteristics and Evolution of AI-usage in GitHub Repositories: Evidence from Code Comments
problem: How developers adapt AI-generated code in real-world projects is not well understood, as prior studies evaluate LLM outputs in isolation rather than examining their integration and evolution in practice.
key_idea: Analyzes 35,361 GitHub code comments referencing AI use and their associated code blocks, along with subsequent commit messages, to derive a taxonomy of AI-assisted development activities and study how AI-assisted code evolves over time.
method: Open-coded 500 unique comments and code blocks to derive a taxonomy, then annotated the full dataset using two LLM-based classifiers with Dawid-Skene expectation-maximization. Analyzed 12,996 subsequent commit messages and temporal trends from December 2022 to March 2026.
dataset_or_scenario: 35,361 GitHub code comments referencing AI use and their associated code blocks, plus 12,996 subsequent commit messages.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (qualitative analysis with taxonomy and temporal trends).
results_summary: Developers primarily use LLMs for code implementation, followed by enhancement, debugging, documentation, and testing. Subsequent commits involve refactoring, feature integration, and bug fixing. Over time, AI-referencing comments shift from direct code generation toward knowledge support and code enhancement.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on explicit AI references in comments, which may not capture all AI usage, and generalizability beyond GitHub.

title: SkelDPO: A Skeleton-Guided Direct Preference Optimization Framework for Efficient Code Generation
problem: Existing Code LLMs treat full programs as a single optimization target during training, failing to model structural factors that influence execution efficiency, leading to generated code that is semantically correct but not efficient.
key_idea: Introduces skeleton-guided preference optimization that identifies efficiency-prone and inefficiency-prone points in code through comparative analysis, forming alignment signals between efficient and inefficient skeletons.
method: SkelDPO first identifies efficient and inefficient implementations from code datasets, locates their efficiency-prone and inefficiency-prone points via comparative analysis, and uses a joint code and skeleton preference loss during training to reinforce understanding of efficiency-critical components.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Pass@1, Beyond@1, Effi@1
results_summary: SkelDPO surpasses existing methods, improving Pass@1, Beyond@1, and Effi@1 by 3-6%, 3-7%, and 2-5% respectively compared to SOTA, with greater improvements on complex tasks.

title: Chiseling Out Efficiency: Structured Skeleton Supervision for Efficient Code Generation
problem: LLMs generate functionally correct but inefficient code; existing methods lack explicit encoding of structural patterns for runtime performance.
key_idea: Proposes efficiency skeletons—abstract, reusable structural patterns—to explicitly model efficiency-oriented code structures.
method: Extracts efficiency skeletons via three complementary strategies and integrates them into a multi-task learning regime that jointly optimizes code generation and skeleton prediction.
dataset_or_scenario: Multiple programming languages and benchmarks, including Mercury.
metrics: Efficiency Ratio (ER) and Average Speedup (AS).
results_summary: EffiSkel achieves +11.11% ER vs. EffiCoder and +3.71% vs. CodeDPO, and +0.36 AS vs. EffiCoder and +0.22 vs. CodeDPO on Mercury with DeepSeek-Coder (7B).

title: Agentic Large Language Models for Automated Structural Analysis of 3D Frame Systems
problem: Extending agentic LLMs to automated structural analysis of 3D frames is underexplored due to challenges in irregular geometric representation, topological consistency, and long-horizon reasoning.
key_idea: Representing irregular 3D frames by projection onto a 2D plan with orthogonal gridlines and a matrix of story numbers, and using a multi-agent pipeline for task decomposition.
method: A multi-agent pipeline including problem analysis, floor decomposition, node/girder/slab/column agents, support/load agents, and code translation agents to generate SAP2000 scripts from natural language.
dataset_or_scenario: Ten representative 3D frames.
metrics: Average accuracy across repeated trials.
results_summary: The framework achieves an average accuracy of 90% across repeated trials on ten representative 3D frames.

title: Multi-LCB: Extending LiveCodeBench to Multiple Programming Languages
problem: LiveCodeBench (LCB) is restricted to Python, leaving the question of whether LLMs can generalize across diverse programming languages required in real-world software engineering.
key_idea: Introducing Multi-LCB, a benchmark that transforms Python tasks from LCB into equivalent tasks in twelve programming languages while preserving contamination controls and evaluation protocol.
method: Multi-LCB transforms Python tasks from the LCB dataset into equivalent tasks in twelve programming languages, maintaining LCB's contamination controls and evaluation protocol, and is fully compatible with the original LCB format to track future updates.
dataset_or_scenario: Multi-LCB benchmark covering twelve programming languages, derived from LiveCodeBench (LCB) dataset.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Evaluation of 24 LLMs on Multi-LCB uncovered evidence of Python overfitting, language-specific contamination, and substantial disparities in multilingual performance.

title: Repository-Level Solidity Code Generation with Large Language Models: From Prompting to Fine-Tuning
problem: Existing benchmarks and metrics are insufficient for repository-level Solidity code generation, where models must synthesize complete contracts from natural language requirements while satisfying strict language-level, security, and software-engineering constraints.
key_idea: Introduction of SolidityBench, a benchmark of 5,470 repository-level Solidity smart contracts with natural language descriptions, and SolidityScore, a Solidity-aware semantic metric emphasizing domain-critical constructs.
method: Evaluated representative code LLMs (Qwen2.5-Coder, DeepSeek-Coder, CodeLlama) across zero-shot prompting, Chain-of-Thought reasoning, in-context learning, retrieval-augmented generation, and supervised fine-tuning on the new benchmark.
dataset_or_scenario: SolidityBench: 5,470 repository-level Solidity smart contracts paired with natural language descriptions.
metrics: SolidityScore (a Solidity-aware semantic metric) and presumably other standard metrics (not explicitly listed).
results_summary: General-purpose models show systematic structural deficiencies; retrieval-augmented generation performs best among non-parametric methods, while supervised fine-tuning achieves the largest improvement by internalizing Solidity-specific constraints.

title: JAMER: Project-Level Code Framework Dataset and Benchmark on Professional Game Engines
problem: Project-level code engineering on professional game engines remains unexplored due to lack of large-scale datasets and deterministic evaluation methods.
key_idea: Leveraging Game Jam competitions to obtain thousands of open-source projects, and using Godot engine's text-based format and headless execution for deterministic verification.
method: Constructed JamSet and JamBench by distilling 8,133 verified projects from over 240,000 repositories via a deterministic verification pipeline; defined theme-driven generation and code completion tasks evaluated by compilation pass rates, Structural Completeness Score (SCS), and Behavioral Alignment Score (BAS).
dataset_or_scenario: JamSet (7,833 projects) and JamBench (300 manually verified projects) built on Godot engine; tasks include theme-driven generation and code completion.
metrics: Compilation pass rates, Structural Completeness Score (SCS), Behavioral Alignment Score (BAS), runtime pass rates.
results_summary: Evaluation of 9 frontier models shows a capability cliff: runtime pass rates drop from 80.4% on small projects to 5.7% on large ones; Code Agents improve compilation but not runtime behavior, indicating architectural design bottleneck.

title: Prompt Quality and Pull Request Outcomes: A Stage-Based Empirical Study of LLM-Assisted Development
problem: The role of prompt structure in collaborative integration behavior within LLM-assisted software engineering workflows is insufficiently understood.
key_idea: Prompt structure is operationalized using three dimensions (Context, Specificity, Verification) and shown to have distinct, stage-dependent effects on pull request outcomes.
method: Analyzed 265 manually validated developer-ChatGPT interactions from open-source pull requests, using a hybrid human-LLM annotation strategy to evaluate prompt structure dimensions and their association with code generation, adoption, and integration depth.
dataset_or_scenario: 265 manually validated developer-ChatGPT interactions derived from self-admitted ChatGPT usage in open-source pull requests.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Specificity and Context are most strongly associated with actionable code generation; Verification predicts code adoption; Context is most associated with integration depth.

title: Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis
problem: The research problem is the difficulty in comparing the capabilities and trade-offs of various Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) due to differences in evaluation protocols, datasets, inference budgets, and generation hyperparameters.
key_idea: The core novelty is a systematic experimental analysis that evaluates eight state-of-the-art DLMs across diverse benchmarks while explicitly considering both generation quality and computational efficiency, and analyzing the impact of key inference-time factors.
method: The method involves evaluating eight state-of-the-art DLMs across eight benchmarks covering reasoning, coding, translation, knowledge, and structured problem solving, along with controlled comparisons of smaller models trained under identical conditions and analysis of inference-time factors like denoising steps, context length, block size, and parallel unmasking strategies.
dataset_or_scenario: Eight benchmarks spanning reasoning, coding, translation, knowledge, and structured problem solving.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (likely generation quality and computational efficiency metrics).
results_summary: The analysis highlights that DLM behavior is strongly influenced by generation-time design choices, leading to distinct trade-offs between performance and computational efficiency, providing practical insights into capabilities and deployment characteristics.

title: Explaining Attention with Program Synthesis
problem: How to replace opaque neural computations in deep networks with human-meaningful symbolic descriptions, specifically for attention heads in transformer language models.
key_idea: Use program synthesis to generate Python programs that reproduce attention patterns of transformer heads, enabling symbolic transparency.
method: Compute attention matrices for a head on random examples, prompt a pre-trained language model to generate Python programs from matrix summaries, then re-rank programs by prediction accuracy on held-out inputs.
dataset_or_scenario: TinyStories dataset for evaluation; GPT-2, TinyLlama-1.1B, and Llama-3B models.
metrics: Intersection-over-Union similarity, perplexity increase, downstream QA performance.
results_summary: Fewer than 1,000 generated programs achieve >75% IoU similarity on TinyStories; replacing 25% of attention heads with programs incurs only 16% average perplexity increase while maintaining QA performance.

title: Generating Natural and Expressive Robot Gestures through Iterative Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback using LLMs
problem: Generating natural and expressive robot gestures remains challenging due to reliance on expert-authored animations or machine learning approaches that struggle with perceived naturalness, especially for robots with many degrees of freedom.
key_idea: Integrating ChatGPT into a humanoid robot for co-speech gesture generation and using iterative reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) to fine-tune gesture generation based on user evaluations.
method: The system uses ChatGPT to generate co-speech gestures for the Pepper robot, then applies an iterative RLHF system that refines gesture generation based on user feedback from an iterative user study.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: RLHF improved the LLM's co-speech generative capabilities, producing more expressive, relevant, and fluid movements compared to the baseline.
limitations: The abstract does not specify limitations, but the baseline gestures were perceived as stiff and unnatural, suggesting that further refinement may be needed.

title: From Specification to Execution: AI Assisted Scientific Workflow Management
problem: Scientific workflow design, implementation, and debugging remain largely manual and require significant expertise, and existing LLM-based approaches rely on direct code synthesis, limiting transparency and integration with workflow systems.
key_idea: Introduces a structured specification phase that separates workflow intent, design, and implementation, enabling validation before code generation, and integrates an LLM-based debugging agent with a Model Context Protocol layer for distributed execution.
method: Combines specification-driven workflow generation, automated debugging via an LLM-based agent, and distributed execution using Pegasus WMS with an MCP layer for unified user interaction.
dataset_or_scenario: A federated learning workflow for medical imaging, chosen for its parallel, iterative, and dependency-intensive structure.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (mentions reduced debugging effort and generation of large-scale workflows with thousands of jobs).
results_summary: The system generated and executed large-scale workflows with thousands of jobs, reduced debugging effort, and allowed non-expert users to construct workflows with expert-level design patterns.

title: LoopCoder-v2: Only Loop Once for Efficient Test-Time Computation Scaling
problem: Looped Transformers scale latent computation by repeatedly applying shared blocks, but sequential looping increases latency and KV-cache memory with loop count. The study addresses how to select the optimal loop count for parallel loop Transformers (PLT) considering a gain-cost trade-off.
key_idea: The core insight is that PLT loop-count selection involves a gain-cost view: an extra loop may refine representations, but cross-loop position offsets (CLP) introduce a positional mismatch at each loop boundary, leading to a non-monotonic effect where two loops are optimal.
method: The authors train LoopCoder-v2, a family of 7B PLT coders with different loop counts, from scratch on 18T tokens, followed by matched instruction tuning and evaluation. They analyze the gain-cost trade-off through diagnostics on representational diversity and CLP-induced mismatch.
dataset_or_scenario: Code generation, code reasoning, agentic software engineering, and tool-use benchmarks, including SWE-bench Verified and Multi-SWE.
metrics: Performance metrics on SWE-bench Verified (43.0 to 64.4 points) and Multi-SWE (14.0 to 31.0 points), along with diagnostics on representational diversity and oscillation.
results_summary: The two-loop variant significantly outperforms the non-looped baseline, improving SWE-bench Verified from 43.0 to 64.4 and Multi-SWE from 14.0 to 31.0, while variants with three or more loops regress, showing a non-monotonic loop-count effect.
limitations: The study is limited to 7B models and specific benchmarks; the gain-cost trade-off may vary with model scale or task types. The CLP-induced mismatch is not fully mitigated.

title: VoidPadding: Let [VOID] Handle Padding in Masked Diffusion Language Models so that [EOS] Can Focus on Semantic Termination
problem: Existing MDLMs assign a dual role to [EOS] as both a semantic terminator and a padding token, causing [EOS] overflow under large-block decoding.
key_idea: Introduce a dedicated [VOID] token for padding, decoupling it from [EOS] which is reserved solely for termination, enabling early stopping and adaptive response canvas expansion.
method: Propose VoidPadding, which uses [VOID] for padding during instruction tuning and inference, while [EOS] signals semantic termination; learned signals guide early stopping and adaptive canvas expansion.
dataset_or_scenario: Mathematical reasoning and code generation benchmarks, evaluated on Dream-7B-Instruct.
metrics: Block-size-averaged four-task mean, decoding NFE (number of function evaluations).
results_summary: VoidPadding improves the four-task mean by +17.84 points over the original model and +6.95 points over RainbowPadding, while reducing decoding NFE by 55.7% on average.

title: FllumaOne: A Code-Native Multimodal CAD Dataset with Executable Programs and Kernel-Validated Feature Histories
problem: Existing CAD datasets lack executable programs with validated geometry and structured feature histories, limiting research in editable CAD and program synthesis.
key_idea: Introduces a code-native multimodal CAD dataset where models are generated by executable Python programs in a CAD system, with kernel-validated geometry and aligned multimodal representations.
method: Generates 100,000 CAD samples using executable Python programs in Flluma, a Qt/C++ OpenCASCADE-based system, with kernel validation, modality completeness checks, and duplicate tests. A Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B LoRA baseline is trained on 80,000 samples.
dataset_or_scenario: FllumaOne-100K dataset with 100,000 samples across four complexity regimes, including programs, feature trees, STEP geometry, point clouds, descriptions, metadata, and renderings.
metrics: Python syntax validity (99.98%), Flluma build success (99.97%), STEP-export validity (99.14%), mean normalized Chamfer Distance (0.002124).
results_summary: The baseline model achieves high validity rates and low Chamfer Distance on the test split, demonstrating the dataset's utility for program synthesis and CAD reconstruction.

title: Bridging Functional Correctness and Runtime Efficiency Gaps in LLM-Based Code Translation
problem: LLM-translated programs often run slower than human-written ones, and this runtime efficiency issue cannot be remedied through prompt engineering alone.
key_idea: Proposes SwiftTrans, a framework with Multi-Perspective Exploration using parallel in-context learning and Difference-Aware Selection to optimize both correctness and runtime efficiency.
method: SwiftTrans comprises two stages: (1) Multi-Perspective Exploration with MpTranslator using parallel ICL to generate diverse candidates; (2) Difference-Aware Selection with DiffSelector comparing differences to pick the optimal candidate. Hierarchical and Ordinal Guidance are introduced for LLM adaptation.
dataset_or_scenario: Extended CodeNet and F2SBench, and introduced SwiftBench.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: SwiftTrans achieves consistent improvements in both correctness and runtime efficiency across all three benchmarks.

title: PracRepair: LLM-Empowered Automated Program Repair Inspired by Human-Like Debugging Practices
problem: Existing LLM-based APR approaches underutilize dynamic information for failure understanding and repair, such as failure-execution traces and patch-validation dynamics, which are noisy, large, and not self-explanatory.
key_idea: Inspired by human debugging practices, PracRepair constructs on-demand static-dynamic context, performs question-driven failure diagnosis to formulate explicit repair hypotheses, and iteratively refines patches using validation diagnostics and trace-level behavioral changes.
method: PracRepair is a fully automated LLM-based APR framework that builds static-dynamic context from buggy programs and failure executions, uses question-driven diagnosis to generate repair hypotheses, and iteratively improves candidate patches with validation feedback and trace-level changes.
dataset_or_scenario: Defects4J V1.2 and V2.0, and RWB (Real-World Bugs).
metrics: Number of correctly fixed bugs.
results_summary: Under GPT-3.5, PracRepair fixes 139/136 bugs on Defects4J V1.2/V2.0; under GPT-4o, it fixes 162/171. It also achieves best performance on RWB across multiple foundation models.

title: Unlocking LLM Code Correction with Iterative Feedback Loops
problem: Existing evaluations of LLMs for code generation focus on single-attempt accuracy, overlooking the iterative refinement process central to real-world programming.
key_idea: Systematic investigation of LLMs' ability to rectify their own code through iterative execution feedback, introducing metrics to evaluate code failures and rectification patterns.
method: Uses an iterative refinement framework where LLMs receive compiler error messages and test case feedback after each attempt, evaluating performance across four models and two programming languages.
dataset_or_scenario: Real-world programming problems across four models and two major programming languages.
metrics: Metrics to evaluate code failures, rectification patterns, and comparison of reasoning vs. non-reasoning models.
results_summary: Reasoning models consistently improve over iterations, substantially outperforming non-reasoning models in leveraging feedback; syntactic and runtime errors are more tractable than logical or algorithmic failures.

title: No Resource, No Benchmarks, No Problem? Evaluating and Improving LLMs for Code Generation in No-Resource Languages
problem: The research addresses the challenge of code generation for no-resource languages, which are proprietary or domain-specific languages with virtually no training data available for LLMs.
key_idea: The core novelty is the introduction of three code generation benchmarks for no-resource languages and a method to adapt LLMs via further pre-training on limited data followed by weight diff transfer from an instruction model to preserve instruction-following capabilities.
method: The authors build and release three code generation benchmarks for no-resource languages. They experiment with prompt-based techniques, pre-training, and fine-tuning using limited data. They propose starting from a base model, further pre-training on the target language, then injecting instruction-following capabilities via weight diff transfer from an instruction model.
dataset_or_scenario: Three code generation benchmarks for no-resource languages, based on two recently proposed programming languages with very little training data.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Further pre-training gives the largest performance gains for no-resource languages, but applying it directly to instruction-tuned models harms instruction-following. The proposed approach significantly improves code generation in no-resource settings, enabling cheap deployment of specialized instruct models.
limitations: The approach relies on the availability of a base model and an instruction model, and the weight diff transfer method may not generalize to all no-resource languages.

title: LLM-based Visual Code Completion for Aerospace Geometric Design
problem: The aerospace industry lacks LLM-based geometric design copilot systems due to safety and explainability concerns, and no such system is in commercial use by aerospace OEMs.
key_idea: A visual programming copilot using a ReAct methodology with GPT 5.4, along with a new Grasshopper plugin library (Wingbuilder) and an Aerospace Visual Programming Dataset (AVPD) for aerospace-specific geometry tasks.
method: The copilot employs a visual programming variant of the ReAct methodology with GPT 5.4, integrated with Wingbuilder plugin for aerospace geometry abstraction, and evaluated via a user trial with two aerospace engineers.
dataset_or_scenario: Aerospace Visual Programming Dataset (AVPD) with 18 aerospace expert designed tasks at different difficulty levels with ground truth solutions.
metrics: User trial feedback on helpfulness and willingness to use; inference time noted as a limitation.
results_summary: The copilot generated helpful suggestions, but slow ReAct inference times limit usefulness to complex tasks; participants liked the tool and would use it in the future.
limitations: Slow ReAct inference times limit usefulness to simpler tasks; evaluation only with two engineers, limiting generalizability.

title: REFLEX: Reflective Evolution from LLM Experience
problem: Existing evolutionary search frameworks using LLMs entangle visual diagnosis and code generation, creating opaque feedback loops and preventing retention of algorithmic insights across runs.
key_idea: Structurally decoupling visual diagnosis from code generation to enable auditable mutation traces and cross-run knowledge transfer via a persistent Skill Memory.
method: REFLEX uses a vision-enabled Critic to distill behavioral evidence into structured diagnoses, then a text-optimized Actor synthesizes child policies using diagnoses and a self-evolving Skill Memory of reusable code snippets.
dataset_or_scenario: Control benchmarks (Lunar Lander, Acrobot, Pendulum) and a 36-dimensional antenna array synthesis task.
metrics: Sample efficiency (LLM calls to solve), Best Normalized Weighted Score.
results_summary: REFLEX solves Acrobot and Pendulum in under 10 LLM calls and achieves a best Normalized Weighted Score of 1.092 on Lunar Lander, showing highly competitive final performance and accelerated early-stage discovery.

title: SPARK: Security Knowledge Priming and Representation-Guided Knowledge Activation for LLM-based Secure Code Generation
problem: Large language models routinely generate code with exploitable security flaws, and existing defenses rely on heavy fine-tuning or external knowledge retrieval, which introduce computational overhead and data bias.
key_idea: Pretraining corpora already contain sufficient security knowledge; the bottleneck is activation, which can be achieved via a brief structured cue and a precomputed token bias without retraining.
method: SPARK has two components: Component I retrieves relevant CWE entries and appends a short structured cue to the prompt; Component II adds a precomputed token bias (safe-direction vector) to logits at each decoding step, computed once offline.
dataset_or_scenario: Evaluated on 9 open-source models across C++, Java, and Python, and tested on 7 strong models (Claude, DeepSeek, GPT) in a black-box setting.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (mentions matching or improving on best baseline while preserving HumanEval utility).
results_summary: SPARK matches or improves on the best baseline in every setting while preserving HumanEval utility, and demonstrates improvements in black-box settings on strong models.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on precomputed bias and CWE retrieval quality.

title: Binary Decompilation LLM with Feedback-Driven Multi-Turn Refinement
problem: Existing LLM-based binary decompilation methods follow a single-turn generation paradigm, producing code that may appear readable but deviates from the original binary's behavior, misleading downstream analysis.
key_idea: Formulating binary decompilation as an iterative refinement process using reinforcement learning with feedback from compilation, execution, and input/output testing.
method: AutoDecompiler uses reinforcement learning with decompilation-specific rewards (code validity, recompilability, execution consistency, semantic fidelity) and stage-aware diagnostic feedback, along with progress-aware trajectory rewarding and turn-aware advantage reweighting.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Behavioral re-executability
results_summary: AutoDecompiler consistently outperforms single-turn counterparts under the same model size and input setting, achieving clear improvements in behavioral re-executability.

title: Know Your Limits : On the Faithfulness of LLMs as Solvers and Autoformalizers in Legal Reasoning
problem: The paper investigates whether LLMs' strong performance on legal reasoning tasks reflects faithful logical inference or heuristic approximation, specifically in legal entailment.
key_idea: The study reveals a systematic gap between pragmatic legal interpretation and strict formal entailment, and identifies failure modes like scope laundering that undermine the faithfulness of LLM-based formal reasoning.
method: Three paradigms are compared: pure LLM classification, LLM-based Formal Reasoning, and solver-based Formal Reasoning using the Z3 SMT solver, on a re-annotated subset of ContractNLI across five LLMs.
dataset_or_scenario: A re-annotated subset of ContractNLI, a legal entailment dataset.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (likely accuracy or benchmark performance).
results_summary: LLM-based Formal Reasoning achieves the highest benchmark performance, but this gain does not imply faithful reasoning; scope laundering persists across all models, indicating a gap between accuracy and logical faithfulness.
limitations: The study is limited to legal entailment and a specific dataset; the identified failure modes may not generalize to other domains or tasks.

title: Beyond NL2Code: A Structured Survey of Multimodal Code Intelligence
problem: Real programming tasks often specify intent through visual artifacts (e.g., screenshots, charts, videos), requiring models to connect visual perception to executable programs beyond text-to-code synthesis.
key_idea: The paper provides a structured survey of Multimodal Code Intelligence, formulating the field by the role code plays (e.g., rendered artifact, editable structure, scientific representation) and organizing benchmarks/methods into four domains.
method: The survey categorizes tasks and approaches into four domains: Graphical User Interface, Scientific Visualization, Structured Graphics, and Frontier Tasks and Frameworks, and proposes four verification-centered future directions.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Not specified in the abstract

title: Mean-Field Parallel Decoding for Discrete Diffusion Language Models
problem: Discrete diffusion language models suffer from limited parallelism due to independent token selection by marginal confidence, leading to incompatible configurations when multiple positions are updated simultaneously.
key_idea: A training-free decoding framework that coordinates parallel updates by assigning commit scores to masked positions and refining them using pairwise interactions derived from the model's predictive distributions, with a variational relaxation yielding a fixed-point update.
method: The method assigns a commit score to each masked position and refines these scores using pairwise interactions from the model's predictive distributions, employing a variational relaxation to derive a simple fixed-point update that suppresses conflicting commitments within a single forward pass.
dataset_or_scenario: Reasoning and code-generation benchmarks.
metrics: Quality-latency trade-off (specific metrics not named in abstract).
results_summary: The method shows consistent improvements in the quality-latency trade-off on reasoning and code-generation benchmarks.

title: LLM4RTL: Tool-Assisted LLM for RTL Generation
problem: The research addresses the need for high-quality training samples to build specialized LLM systems for open Verilog/RTL code generation, and identifies weaknesses of LLMs in rule-based reasoning and logic for RTL code generation.
key_idea: Proposes a 'judge-renew-check-renew-check' (JRCRC) pipeline to filter and refine code-generation samples into a higher-quality training dataset, and develops a tool-assisted architecture to dynamically assist LLMs in inferring logical relationships from tabular data.
method: The JRCRC pipeline uses a hierarchy of commercial LLMs with different costs and capabilities to update a public dataset. A tool-assisted architecture is developed to incorporate pre-processing tools that help LLMs infer logical relationships from tabular data formats.
dataset_or_scenario: VerilogEval benchmark
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (likely pass@k or similar, but not stated)
results_summary: The LLM4RTL system achieves significant overall performance gains on the VerilogEval benchmark, outperforming many state-of-the-art methods and achieving performance comparable to GPT-4O using a significantly smaller LLM.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; common weaknesses of LLMs in rule-based reasoning and logic are identified but not detailed.

title: A Spatio-Temporal Expert Prefetching Framework for Efficient MoE-based LLM Inference
problem: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) based LLMs suffer from expert loading latency during inference due to dynamic and irregular expert activation patterns, causing performance and energy inefficiency.
key_idea: Expert requests exhibit strong spatio-temporal correlation across adjacent MoE layers and consecutive decoding tokens, enabling predictable future expert activations for prefetching.
method: Proposes ST-MoE, a spatio-temporal expert prefetching framework combining a lightweight runtime prediction mechanism that preserves original routing behavior with a reconfigurable hardware design for dynamic expert prefetching.
dataset_or_scenario: Various MoE-based LLMs and applications including language understanding and code generation.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: ST-MoE significantly improves MoE inference performance and energy efficiency while preserving model inference accuracy.

title: AI-driven Software Development: A Pragmatic Path to Agentic Development Processes
problem: The paper addresses the challenge of transitioning from localized AI tool support to fully integrated AI-driven software development processes, focusing on technical, organizational, and quality-assurance mechanisms.
key_idea: Proposes a pragmatic organizing framework for progressing from informal AI use through integrated workflows to controlled agentic development processes, emphasizing a harness for project context, tool access, verification, permissions, logging, and human approval.
method: The framework is developed based on current research, practice-oriented sources, established software engineering practices, and project experience, and is assessed via an exploratory case study in a mid-sized software company.
dataset_or_scenario: A mid-sized software company used as an exploratory case study.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: The case study illustrates how prerequisites, governance requirements, design practices, and transformation paths can be shaped in a concrete organizational context, providing a conceptual basis for further discussion and empirical investigation.
limitations: The framework is based on a single exploratory case study, and its generalizability may be limited; further empirical investigation is needed.

title: Driving, Fast or Slow? Neuro-Symbolic Guidance for Motion Prediction in Multi-Modal Ground Mobility
problem: Accurate and interpretable motion prediction for heterogeneous traffic spaces is essential for safe autonomous navigation, but state-of-the-art approaches lack explicit encoding of regulatory and behavioral constraints.
key_idea: TraCS augments black-box motion prediction backbones with interpretable probabilistic first-order logic using an agentic code-generation pipeline and a reactive data-streaming inference engine.
method: TraCS uses an agentic code-generation pipeline to translate natural-language traffic regulations into probabilistic logic, and a reactive inference engine to maintain compliance landscapes. A neural confidence rating learns context-aware attenuation of the compliance signal.
dataset_or_scenario: Argoverse 2 benchmark
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: TraCS consistently improves state-of-the-art prediction backbones on Argoverse 2, showing that probabilistic and symbolic compliance reasoning is a broadly applicable and computationally efficient complement to neural predictors.

title: TriAdReview: Triangular Adversarial Review Architecture for Multi-Model Technical Document Generation
problem: Single-model outputs for technical document generation often suffer from over-engineering, security blind spots, and incomplete coverage.
key_idea: A triangular adversarial review architecture with two independent reviewer models and a triangular judging mechanism to iteratively improve generator output.
method: TriAdReview uses two reviewer models (engineering and boundary perspectives) and a triangular judging mechanism to iteratively refine a generator model's output across multiple tasks.
dataset_or_scenario: Five benchmark tasks: architecture design, code generation, proposal review, security audit, and requirements analysis.
metrics: Overall score out of 50, p-value from paired t-test, and inter-rater agreement.
results_summary: Triple model configuration achieves 10.1% overall improvement over baseline (26.2 vs. 23.8 out of 50; p<0.05), with strong gains on security audit (+27.6%), code generation (+20.8%), and architecture design (+15.6%), but a -7.5% degradation on requirements analysis.
limitations: The system shows a structural bias toward simplification, causing degradation on completeness-oriented tasks like requirements analysis; reviewer prompt adaptation only partially mitigates this.

title: Rumoca: Modelica as a Universal Algebraic Frontend via a Rust-Native Compiler
problem: Modelica models must be rewritten or lose information when used in modern engineering workflows like optimization and differentiable simulation, as existing toolchains do not target these environments directly.
key_idea: Rumoca compiles Modelica into a universal algebraic frontend that can target multiple backends (CasADi, JAX, Julia) via a Rust-native compiler with explicit phase boundaries and template-driven code generation.
method: The compiler is organized as a sequence of phases from parsing through DAE construction to template-driven code generation, with a native Rust simulation backend supporting real-time and software-in-the-loop execution.
dataset_or_scenario: Modelica Standard Library coverage, compile-time and simulation-time benchmarks against an open-source reference, and end-to-end case studies including quadrotor control.
metrics: Quantitative coverage of Modelica Standard Library across pipeline phases, compile-time and simulation-time benchmarks.
results_summary: The compiler achieves quantitative coverage of the Modelica Standard Library and demonstrates competitive compile-time and simulation-time performance against an open-source reference, with successful real-time control of a quadrotor model.

title: Beyond Correctness: Enhancing Architectural Reasoning in Code LLMs via Scalable Labeling with Agentic Judgment
problem: LLMs lack architectural understanding in software engineering, which is expensive to label manually and impossible to verify through tests alone.
key_idea: Use a strong LLM as a scalable proxy for expert architectural evaluation via two judges: Architecture Complexity Judge (ACJ) and Architecture Quality Judge (AQJ).
method: Propose an agentic judging pipeline with ACJ estimating task complexity and AQJ evaluating patch conformance to architectural conventions, then fine-tune Qwen3-8B/14B/32B on 3,360 curated instances.
dataset_or_scenario: SWE-bench Verified
metrics: Resolved rates
results_summary: Fine-tuned models achieve resolved rates up to 27.2% on SWE-bench Verified, up to 540% over base model and 256% over unfiltered fine-tuning, with strong cross-language generalization.

title: Towards Direct Latent-Space Synthesis for Parallel Branches in LLM-Agent Workflows
problem: Existing LLM-agent systems merge parallel branches by concatenating textual outputs, which discards parallel structure and incurs redundant prefill computation.
key_idea: Introduces Parallel-Synthesis, a framework that enables a synthesizer to directly consume KV caches from parallel worker agents, bypassing text concatenation.
method: Parallel-Synthesis uses a cache mapper to calibrate independently generated branch caches and a fine-tuned synthesizer adapter for generation from non-sequential cache interface; trained with data exposing synthesizer to parallel cache contexts and distilling reasoning from text-concatenation synthesis.
dataset_or_scenario: Nine downstream datasets spanning math, science QA, code generation, GAIA, and multi-agent database diagnosis.
metrics: Time-to-first-token, performance comparison (matches or outperforms text-based synthesis on seven datasets).
results_summary: Parallel-Synthesis matches or outperforms text-based synthesis on seven of nine datasets and reduces time-to-first-token by 2.5x-11x.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require fine-tuning and cache mapper calibration.

title: SemPiper: Interactive Code Synthesis for Semantic Operators in Machine Learning Pipelines
problem: Developing ML pipelines is tedious and error-prone due to extensive data preparation and integration, and chat-based LLM interfaces provide limited control and produce hard-to-optimize code.
key_idea: Introduces SemPipes, a programming model with declarative, LLM-powered semantic operators that synthesize specialized implementations conditioned on dataset and pipeline context.
method: SemPipes allows developers to specify high-level natural language instructions for data operations, which are combined with Python code; implementations are synthesized at training time via evolutionary search.
dataset_or_scenario: Three end-to-end scenarios for attendees to explore, modify pipelines, and inspect generated code.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: The demonstration highlights how declarative semantic operators enable controllable, optimizable, and practical integration of LLMs into ML pipeline development.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on LLM quality and evolutionary search efficiency.

title: MeEvo: Metacognitive Evolution Combined with Natural Evolution for Automatic Heuristic Design
problem: Existing LLM-based Automatic Heuristic Design (AHD) methods either discard reasoning traces (Natural Evolution) or lack population-level recombination (Metacognitive Evolution), leading to reduced search efficiency, stability, and solution quality on complex problems.
key_idea: Cyclically coupling Natural Evolution and Metacognitive Evolution in a dual-layer framework, where Natural Evolution explores heuristic code and records reasoning traces, and Metacognitive Evolution reflects on this history to generate improved heuristics.
method: MeEvo is a dual-layer AHD framework that alternates between Natural Evolution (exploring heuristic code via crossover/mutation and recording traces, fitness, errors) and Metacognitive Evolution (reflecting on the shared history to generate improved heuristics), which re-enter the parent pool for the next cycle.
dataset_or_scenario: Five optimization problems with two LLM backbones.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (performance and stability are mentioned).
results_summary: MeEvo achieves stronger and more stable performance than existing LLM-based AHD architectures, especially on complex constrained tasks.

title: FastContext: Training Efficient Repository Explorer for Coding Agents
problem: Repository exploration in LLM coding agents is a bottleneck, consuming large token budgets and polluting context with irrelevant snippets.
key_idea: Separating repository exploration from task solving using a dedicated exploration subagent that issues parallel tool calls and returns concise context.
method: FastContext is a specialized exploration subagent powered by models (4B-30B parameters) bootstrapped from reference-model trajectories and refined with task-grounded rewards for broad first-turn search, multi-turn evidence gathering, and precise citation generation.
dataset_or_scenario: SWE-bench Multilingual, SWE-bench Pro, and SWE-QA
metrics: End-to-end resolution rates and token consumption
results_summary: Integrating FastContext into Mini-SWE-Agent improves resolution rates up to 5.5% while reducing token consumption up to 60% with marginal overhead.

title: Adaptive Nucleus Truncation for Long-Form Reasoning
problem: Existing truncation methods for sampling in long-form language model reasoning rely on fixed thresholds that cannot adapt to changes in entropy, task difficulty, training stage, or generation budget.
key_idea: Introduces Adaptive Nucleus Truncation Sampling (ANTS), which extends top-nσ sampling into an adaptive rollout-control mechanism that adjusts truncation width using an entropy-conditioned controller and retains a no-truncation fallback arm.
method: ANTS selects standardized neighborhoods around the maximum logit before temperature scaling, adapts truncation width via an entropy-conditioned controller, and uses a no-truncation fallback to stabilize training when truncation is unsafe.
dataset_or_scenario: Evaluated on a 33B-total / 4B-active sparse Mixture-of-Experts reasoning model across instruction following (IFBench), mathematical reasoning (AIME 2025), and code generation (Codeforces) at 8K, 16K, and 32K generation budgets.
metrics: Average performance improvement in points, IFBench improvement, AIME 2025 improvement, and ELO on Codeforces.
results_summary: ANTS improves average performance over percentage-based benchmarks by +1.9, +3.8, and +5.2 points at 8K, 16K, and 32K budgets, with strongest gains on instruction following (+10 points at 32K) and mathematical reasoning (+7 points on AIME 2025). On Codeforces, ANTS trails at 8K but reverses the gap at 16K and 32K.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; however, the method shows a budget interaction where performance lags at low budgets on code generation, suggesting potential limitations for short-budget tasks.

title: A Benchmark and Framework for Evaluating Next Action Predictions in Spreadsheets
problem: Predictive code completion is common in development but virtually non-existent in spreadsheets, which are more widely used. The challenges are the absence of edit histories in public spreadsheet corpora and the complex space of spreadsheet actions.
key_idea: Introduces a benchmark and online evaluation framework for predicting next user actions in spreadsheets, addressing the lack of edit histories and complex action spaces.
method: Manually curated 52 sequences of 12K actions from public corpora using parametrized heuristics and LLM refinement. Proposed an online evaluation that predicts after each action, accepts/rejects, updates future actions, and repeats until target spreadsheet is obtained.
dataset_or_scenario: 52 sequences of 12K actions curated from public spreadsheet corpora.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (evaluates properties like saved actions, false positives, efficiency, user profiles, triggers, context).
results_summary: Analyzed multiple baseline predictors (zero-shot LLMs, fine-tuned SLMs, classical models) and derived insights on properties such as saved actions, false positives, efficiency, user profiles, triggers, and context.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include the manual curation process and the specific choice of baseline predictors.

title: SEVRA-BENCH: Social Engineering of Vulnerabilities in Review Agents
problem: Automated code reviewers may approve malicious pull requests when attackers control both code changes and accompanying text, a scenario not addressed by existing benchmarks.
key_idea: Introduces a benchmark that inverts real vulnerability fixes to create malicious PRs wrapped in social-engineering framings, testing whether LLM reviewers reject them.
method: Constructs 1,062 malicious PRs by inverting CVE-linked fixes from top CWE entries, each wrapped in one of 15 social-engineering framings, and evaluates 8 LLMs as code review agents.
dataset_or_scenario: 1,062 malicious PRs derived from CVE-linked fixes across top 10 entries of 2025 CWE Top 25.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Reveals a sharp gap in security capabilities between closed- and open-source models.

title: Understanding the Rejection of Fixes Generated by Agentic Pull Requests -- Insights from the AIDev Dataset
problem: AI coding agents generate many pull requests that are rejected (46.41%), leading to wasted human and computational resources; the paper aims to understand the failure modes of these agents.
key_idea: A qualitative and quantitative analysis of rejected AI-agent pull requests to categorize reasons for rejection, providing insights for better integration of AI agents as teammates.
method: Qualitative study on a representative sample of 306 non-merged PRs from the AIDev dataset, followed by quantitative analysis of rejection reasons.
dataset_or_scenario: AIDev dataset containing pull requests generated or co-authored by Copilot, Devin, Cursor, and Claude.
metrics: Rejection rate (46.41%), categories and frequencies of rejection reasons.
results_summary: Identified 14 reasons for rejection grouped into four categories: incorrect implementation, CI pipeline failures, inability to implement, and low priority. Highlights need for better guidance on approach, constraints, and validation.
limitations: The study is based on a single dataset (AIDev) and may not generalize to all AI agents or software projects; sample size of 306 PRs may limit representativeness.

title: Toward Instructions-as-Code: Understanding the Impact of Instruction Files on Agentic Pull Requests
problem: The paper investigates whether instruction files created for AI agents improve the performance of agentic pull requests in terms of merge rate, task complexity, and merge effort.
key_idea: The study reveals that instruction files do not consistently improve agentic PR outcomes; only projects with longer and well-structured instruction files see benefits, motivating the concept of Instructions-as-Code.
method: The authors analyze 15,549 agentic PRs from 148 projects in the AIDev dataset, comparing project metrics before and after the creation of instruction files across three dimensions: merge rate, code churn, and merge effort.
dataset_or_scenario: AIDev dataset containing 15,549 agentic PRs from 148 projects.
metrics: Merge rate, code churn, number of modified files, merge time, number of comments.
results_summary: Only 27.7% of projects increased merge rate by at least 20% after adding instruction files, while 26.35% decreased; similar mixed results were observed for code churn and merge effort. Successful projects had longer, well-structured instruction files.
limitations: The analysis is correlational and based on a specific dataset; causal factors and generalizability to other agent types or tasks are not established.

title: An LLM System for Autonomous Variational Quantum Circuit Design
problem: Designing high-performing quantum circuits remains heavily reliant on human expertise, and there is a need for automated methods to generate quantum circuits under explicit design constraints.
key_idea: An autonomous agentic framework using LLMs to iteratively design quantum circuits through a closed-loop workflow integrating web knowledge, literature critique, code generation, and experimental feedback.
method: The system comprises seven components: Exploration, Generation, Discussion, Validation, Storage, Evaluation, and Review, forming a closed-loop workflow that combines web-based knowledge acquisition, literature-grounded critique, executable code generation, and experimental feedback.
dataset_or_scenario: Two tasks: quantum feature map construction for quantum machine learning (image classification benchmarks) and ansatz generation for variational quantum eigensolver applications in quantum chemistry (seven molecules).
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (implied: classification accuracy, ground state energy accuracy).
results_summary: The best generated feature map outperforms representative quantum feature maps and surpasses the classical radial basis function kernel when scaled; the generated ansatz attains competitive accuracy with chemically inspired and hardware-efficient constructions while satisfying scaling constraints.

title: VHDLSuite: Unified Pipeline for LLM VHDL Generation with Data Synthesis and Evaluation
problem: Evaluating LLM performance for VHDL code generation is limited compared to Verilog, despite VHDL's distinct language characteristics that introduce different evaluation considerations.
key_idea: Introduces VHDLSuite, a benchmark-centered infrastructure for scalable VHDL generation evaluation, integrating automated benchmark synthesis, executable validation, and multi-model diagnostic analysis.
method: Proposes a data pipeline that automatically converts Verilog designs and testbenches into executable VHDL benchmark instances, validated via VUnit/GHDL, and introduces VHDLBench with over 200 VHDL problems with complete testbenches.
dataset_or_scenario: VHDLBench, a benchmark with over 200 VHDL problems across a wide range of complexity levels.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Extensively evaluated cutting-edge LLMs and uncovered key challenges specific to LLM-aided VHDL generation, providing insights for multi-language hardware design automation.

title: Reasoning for Mobile User Experience with Multimodal LLMs: Task, Benchmark, and Approach
problem: Research on evaluating user experience (UX) based on UI screenshots using multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is still immature.
key_idea: Proposes UXBench, a benchmark for UI-based reasoning, and UI-UX, an MLLM enhanced via reinforcement learning with reward routing and asymmetric transition reward.
method: UXBench includes 2,000 VQA samples across 8 tasks for fine-grained UX diagnosis. UI-UX is built on Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking and trained with reinforcement learning using a reward routing mechanism and asymmetric transition reward.
dataset_or_scenario: UXBench benchmark with 2,000 VQA data samples from real-world UI screenshots covering layout, visual hierarchy, and content consistency.
metrics: Accuracy
results_summary: UI-UX achieves state-of-the-art accuracy of 0.7963 on UXBench, surpassing Claude-4.5-Sonnet's 0.6550, with strong generalization and low latency.

title: Structured Testbench Generation for LLM-Driven HDL Design and Verification-Oriented Data Curation
problem: Automated testbench generation in LLM-driven RTL workflows suffers from high token cost, low reproducibility, and insufficient coverage due to unconstrained code synthesis.
key_idea: Exploiting the inherent structure of hardware designs to generate deterministic testbenches, enabling faster, more reliable verification and data curation.
method: STG framework generates structured testbenches by leveraging design structure, achieving deterministic outputs without iterative LLM prompting.
dataset_or_scenario: Multi-benchmark evaluation for RTL generation and verification, including data curation for distilled models.
metrics: Speed (720x faster than iterative LLM flow), compilation success rate, coverage, false-pass verdict reduction, energy efficiency (127x less energy), node count reduction (14-47%).
results_summary: STG achieves 720x faster verification, higher coverage, fewer false passes, and 11x faster data curation with 127x less energy, yielding state-of-the-art distilled models.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require design structure knowledge and may not generalize to all hardware designs.

title: MDForge: Agentic Molecular Dynamics Pipeline Design under Sparse Simulator Feedback
problem: Designing molecular dynamics pipelines for new systems requires expert knowledge and is expensive, ruling out trial-and-error. The paper addresses automating this pipeline design process.
key_idea: Treating pipeline design as open-ended code generation where an LLM agent's behavior is reshaped online by verbal reward, densified via multi-agent debate among physics experts.
method: MDForge uses an LLM agent with an in-context update rule that densifies sparse reward through multi-agent debate among physics experts to design MD pipelines.
dataset_or_scenario: Three SAMPL host-guest binding free-energy benchmarks and a library of unseen candidate guests for CB[7] pipeline.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (competitive with human experts, discovered high-affinity binder).
results_summary: MDForge automatically designs MD pipelines competitive with human experts on benchmarks and discovers a novel picomolar CB[7] binder confirmed by wet-lab competition NMR.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on sparse simulator feedback and generalizability to other MD systems.

title: Beyond Problem Solving: UOJ-Bench for Evaluating Code Generation, Hacking, and Repair in Competitive Programming
problem: The role of LLMs in supporting human learning in competitive programming, particularly in identifying errors in human-written code, remains largely unexplored.
key_idea: Introduces UOJ-Bench, a benchmark with three tasks (code generation, hacking, repair) built from real-world UOJ submissions, evaluated via native judging infrastructure.
method: Constructs benchmark from real UOJ submissions; evaluates LLMs on code generation, hacking (finding errors in human code), and repair; uses one-shot and test-time scaling evaluations.
dataset_or_scenario: UOJ-Bench, built from real-world code submissions on the Universal Online Judge (UOJ).
metrics: Success rates (e.g., identifying errors in incorrect submissions, uncovering errors in full-score submissions).
results_summary: Under one-shot, strongest models fail to identify errors in >50% of incorrect submissions; test-time scaling improves to >90% but with high computational cost. Best models uncover errors in >5% of full-score submissions across ~30 problems.
limitations: High computational cost of test-time scaling limits practicality for large-scale deployment.

title: Token Complexity Theory for AI-Augmented Computing
problem: The paper addresses the lack of a formal resource measure for the cost of sending queries to and receiving responses from AI models in AI-augmented computing, which is not captured by classical time or space complexity.
key_idea: Introduces token complexity as a formal resource measure defined as the minimum expected token cost to achieve a specified output quality, and develops a taxonomy of AI systems based on probabilistic properties.
method: Formalizes token complexity within the framework of AI-Oracle Turing machines, where a probabilistic Turing machine interacts with a stochastic oracle via dedicated query and response tapes, and proves theorems about its properties.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Token complexity (minimum expected token cost), time, space, and the complexity frontier.
results_summary: Proves that token complexity exhibits monotonicity, convexity, price sensitivity, and price-relativity of task ordering, and that the complexity frontier is non-empty, upward-closed, and convex.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; the work is theoretical and may require empirical validation.

title: Shopping Reasoning Bench: An Expert-Authored Benchmark for Multi-Turn Conversational Shopping Assistants
problem: No existing benchmark jointly evaluates the open-ended multi-turn reasoning, domain expertise, and criterion-level quality required for real shopping conversations.
key_idea: Introduces an expert-authored benchmark with importance-weighted binary rubrics organized under a taxonomy of reasoning categories to evaluate shopping assistants.
method: Created 525 missions (232 single-turn, 293 multi-turn) with 10863 importance-weighted binary rubrics authored by retail domain experts, covering five reasoning categories and fifteen subcategories.
dataset_or_scenario: Shopping Reasoning Bench: 525 missions with multi-turn conversational shopping scenarios.
metrics: Pass rates, performance on required vs. optional criteria, and degradation across conversation turns.
results_summary: Nine models (GPT, Claude, Gemini) achieved 57-77% pass rates overall; multi-turn missions showed 13-29 point drops on optional criteria and 4-18 point degradation as conversations progressed.

title: Breaking Entropy Bounds: Accelerating RL Training via MTP with Rejection Sampling
problem: The rollout stage is a key bottleneck in RL training pipelines for LLMs, and MTP acceptance rates degrade during RL training, limiting speedup.
key_idea: MTP acceptance rate is bounded by model entropy fluctuation, and probabilistic rejection sampling alleviates entropy disturbance; a novel end-to-end TV loss directly optimizes multi-step rejection sampling acceptance rate.
method: Proposes Bebop, integrating MTP into RL pipelines with rejection sampling and a novel end-to-end TV loss that optimizes acceptance rate, along with pre-RL MTP training strategies.
dataset_or_scenario: Mathematical reasoning, code generation, and agentic tasks.
metrics: Acceptance rate, inference throughput gains, end-to-end acceleration.
results_summary: Achieves up to 95% acceptance rates, up to 25% extra inference throughput gains, and up to 1.8x end-to-end acceleration in async RL training of Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, and Qwen3.7 models.

title: Agreement in Representation Space for Open-Ended Self-Consistency
problem: Existing self-consistency methods rely on exact matching, limiting them to tasks with categorical outputs; this work addresses self-consistency in open-ended generation tasks like code synthesis and text summarization.
key_idea: Consistency can be understood as a geometric property of the generation space, where semantically compatible generations concentrate in similar regions of representation space.
method: Introduces Embedding-Based Agreement (EBA), a training-free method that estimates agreement by clustering sampled generations in embedding space.
dataset_or_scenario: Mathematical reasoning, code generation, and summarization tasks.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (mentions outperforming random selection and stable scaling behavior).
results_summary: EBA consistently outperforms random selection and exhibits more stable scaling than LLM evaluation or uncertainty estimation; agreement signals remain stable across model families and embedding spaces; generations near central regions of representation space are more reliable.

title: Enhancing LLM-Based Code Translation with Verified Multi-Semantic Representations
problem: LLM-based code translation often relies on token-level patterns rather than program semantics, leading to logical and semantic errors, and high-quality semantic guidance is often unavailable in real-world scenarios.
key_idea: Construct rich semantic information directly from source code and ensure its accuracy through multi-semantic augmentation and self-calibration.
method: Multisage framework with three modules: semantic representation parsing (data-flow graphs, type constraints, API info), multi-semantic augmentation (code summaries, test cases, API descriptions), and semantic consistency calibration (semantics-preserving mutations and cross-semantic verification).
dataset_or_scenario: HumanEval-X code translation benchmark
metrics: Translation success rates
results_summary: Multisage improves translation success rates by up to 2.22 times across diverse backbone models, consistently outperforming vanilla prompting, instruction-tuned LLMs, and Chain-of-Thought reasoning.

title: Grammar-Constrained Decoding Can Jailbreak LLMs into Generating Malicious Code
problem: Large Language Models (LLMs) used for code generation can be misused to produce malicious code, and Grammar-Constrained Decoding (GCD), intended to improve reliability, may inadvertently become an attack surface.
key_idea: The paper reveals that GCD can be exploited to jailbreak LLMs into generating malicious code, and proposes a safety alignment approach called CodeShield to mitigate this vulnerability.
method: CodeSpear exploits GCD by applying benign code grammar constraints to induce malicious code generation. CodeShield aligns the model by teaching it to generate honeypot code under GCD, which is semantically harmless and structurally diverse, while preserving natural-language refusals.
dataset_or_scenario: 10 popular LLMs across 4 benchmarks.
metrics: Attack success rate (ASR) and benign utility preservation.
results_summary: CodeSpear outperforms representative jailbreak baselines, increasing ASR by more than 30 percentage points on average. CodeShield restores safety under CodeSpear while preserving benign utility.

title: CODEBLOCK: Learning to Supervise Code at the Right Granularity
problem: Standard supervised fine-tuning of code LLMs applies uniform loss to all tokens, ignoring that code requires structural completeness and definition-use relations, unlike natural language.
key_idea: Proposes structure-aware sparse supervision that selects syntactically coherent code blocks instead of isolated tokens, preserving program dependencies.
method: CodeBlock selects high-quality instruction-response pairs, partitions code into syntactic blocks, estimates utility via aggregated cross-entropy over core logic tokens, and reranks using data-flow reach and bridge signals; loss is applied only to selected blocks and informative NL tokens.
dataset_or_scenario: Six code-generation benchmarks (not named in abstract).
metrics: pass@1
results_summary: CodeBlock achieves stronger average pass@1 than full-token SFT and competitive baselines, using only 1.9% of supervised response tokens.

title: Counterexample Guided Learning in the Large using Reasoning Agents
problem: LLMs struggle to effectively utilize heterogeneous, domain-specific feedback for improvement, and it is difficult to identify when they can benefit from such feedback.
key_idea: Applying counterexample-guided learning from classical symbolic learning to LLMs for regular-expression induction, where verifier feedback provides precise counterexamples to guide refinement.
method: The approach uses a learner (LLM) to propose candidate regular expressions from labeled strings, and a teacher (verifier) returns counterexamples. Novel strategies include regularization, symbolic counterexample clusters, and agentic reflection/repair loops.
dataset_or_scenario: Challenging regex-induction tasks across two different regex domains.
metrics: Success rate (percentage of tasks solved) and sample efficiency (number of labeled examples required).
results_summary: The counterexample-guided framework substantially improves success rates on hardest tasks from 3.2% to 38.1% and from 38.9% to 74.1% on two domains, reducing required labeled examples.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on precise counterexample generation and applicability to domains beyond regex induction.

title: MPC-Patch-Bench: Security-Aware LLM Code Patch for Multi-Party Computation
problem: No repository-level benchmark exists for evaluating LLM code repair on Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC) software, and general-purpose benchmarks fail due to MPC-specific structural challenges.
key_idea: Introduces MPC-Patch-Bench, a repository-level benchmark with a data curation framework and an MPC verifier that provides security and numerical-fidelity checks.
method: The benchmark includes a data curation framework that filters pull requests through cryptographic layers and synthesizes tests, and an MPC verifier that performs dynamic differential testing and static analysis for security violations.
dataset_or_scenario: 205 fully verified instances from MPC repositories.
metrics: Functional resolution rate and verified resolution rate.
results_summary: The strongest LLM functionally resolves 22.9% of tasks; the MPC Verifier reduces verified resolution to 17.1%, with up to 40% of functionally-passing patches rejected for security violations.

title: An Ocean Model Ported by a Large Language Model: Experience and Lessons from FESOM2 (Fortran to C to C++/Kokkos)
problem: Whether large language models can port a complete, production geophysical model to a different language without degrading its physics has not been established.
key_idea: LLM-assisted code translation can preserve the physics of a complete production ocean model while moving it into a modern performance-portable form, using a two-stage translation process and strict validation.
method: An agentic LLM coding assistant, directed by domain experts, ported the FESOM2 ocean model first from Fortran to C (reproducing numerics) and then from C to C++/Kokkos (introducing parallelism), with literal translation and stage-specific acceptance criteria.
dataset_or_scenario: FESOM2 unstructured mesh ocean–sea-ice model (about 74000 lines of core Fortran), evaluated on eddy-rich meshes up to 7.4 million surface vertices.
metrics: Long-term simulation statistics over five years, bit-for-bit comparison, statistical closeness, and performance (simulated-years-per-day, speedup on GPU vs CPU).
results_summary: The C port reproduces original Fortran statistics over five years; the Kokkos port is bit-for-bit identical on CPU and statistically close on GPU. On a single A100 GPU node, it runs 1.6–3.7 times faster than a CPU node, achieving 1-2 simulated-years-per-day.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract, but the approach required domain expert direction and strict validation; generalizability to other models or languages is not discussed.

title: Mind the Gap: Can Frontier LLMs Pass a Standardized Office Proficiency Exam?
problem: The ability of LLM agents to navigate complex, professional-grade productivity software for office automation is largely untested, requiring long-horizon planning, precise parameter configuration, and multi-application integration.
key_idea: Introduces an evaluation based on China's National Computer Rank Examination (NCRE) with 200 practical-operation tasks across Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, scored on a 100-point rubric with 7,118 machine-gradable criteria.
method: Benchmarks 7 frontier LLMs using single-turn and agentic systems with execution feedback, iterative repair, and broader Office automation access, measuring Score Rate (SR) as mean percentage of rubric points earned.
dataset_or_scenario: 200 comprehensive practical-operation tasks from China's National Computer Rank Examination (NCRE) across Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
metrics: Score Rate (SR) - mean percentage of rubric points earned across tasks.
results_summary: Single-turn models score a maximum of 36.6%, while a stronger agentic system reaches 68.8%, but both remain below the 95.5% community-reference score, indicating significant challenges for current LLM and agent systems.
limitations: The benchmark is limited to Chinese office software tasks and may not generalize to other languages or software; the community-reference score may not reflect real-world human performance.

title: Context-Based Adversarial Attacks on AI Code Generators: Vulnerability Analysis and Implications
problem: AI-powered code generation systems are vulnerable to inference-time security attacks where crafted contextual inputs can bias models to generate exploitable code.
key_idea: Systematic investigation of context-based adversarial attacks and a dual-layer defense framework that achieves high detection with low latency.
method: Conducted 2,800 controlled experiments across CodeT5+, CodeLlama, GPT-3.5-Turbo, and GPT-4, measuring attack effectiveness and defense mechanisms.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Vulnerability generation rate (3.5% to 37.4%), attack success rate (100% for direct instruction on GPT-3.5-Turbo), cross-model transferability (60-100%), defense detection rate (89.1%), false positive rate (0.3%), latency (520ms).
results_summary: Adversarial conditions increase vulnerability generation 10.7x, with direct instruction attacks achieving 100% success on GPT-3.5-Turbo; the dual-layer defense achieves 89.1% detection with 0.3% false positives and 520ms latency.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may include limited model scope or synthetic attack scenarios.

title: A Constrained Natural-Language Interface for Variational Multi-Physics Finite Element Simulations in FEniCS
problem: Large language models can reduce manual effort in setting up finite element simulations but introduce reliability risks when generated solver code lies on the critical path.
key_idea: Constraining the LLM to front-end tasks (parsing prompts, generating geometry code) while using a deterministic dispatcher to map validated specifications to human-written solver templates, avoiding LLM-generated solver code.
method: The system uses an LLM for parsing natural-language prompts into structured JSON and generating Gmsh code for non-catalog geometries, with retry feedback. A deterministic dispatcher selects from five human-written FEniCS/UFL templates (linear elasticity, hyperelasticity, elastoplasticity, thermo-mechanical coupling, phase-field fracture).
