dataset_or_scenario: 15-prompt parser benchmark, 10-case custom-geometry benchmark, and an end-to-end 3D elastoplastic L-bracket demonstration.
metrics: First-pass valid parse rate, final valid parse rate, problem-class accuracy, field-extraction accuracy, first-pass and final success rate for geometry generation.
results_summary: Parser achieved 100% final valid parse rate, 100% problem-class accuracy, and 97.1% field-extraction accuracy. Geometry generation had 90% first-pass and final success rate. Solver templates validated against analytical solutions and benchmarks, with sub-percent to 2-5% agreement.
limitations: Limited to five predefined physics templates; custom-geometry generation had one unrecovered failure; not open-ended autonomous code generation.

title: Securing Code Understanding: Detecting Natural Backdoor Vulnerability in Code Language Models
problem: The security implications of natural backdoor vulnerabilities in Code Language Models (CodeLMs) are poorly understood, despite posing serious threats similar to those from data poisoning.
key_idea: Natural backdoors are prevalent and intrinsic to CodeLMs, differing from injected backdoors at model and parameter levels, and can be detected via a novel method ScanNBT.
method: Empirical study across 44 scenarios examining natural backdoor vulnerabilities in various CodeLM architectures and code intelligence tasks, analyzing transferability from three perspectives and causes from two aspects, and evaluating existing defenses.
dataset_or_scenario: 44 scenarios across various model architectures and code intelligence tasks.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract.
results_summary: Natural backdoors are prevalent and intrinsic to CodeLMs; differences between injected and natural backdoors are revealed; existing defenses are evaluated; ScanNBT improves detection.

title: Self-Distillation Policy Optimization via Visual Feedback: Bridging Code and Visual Artifacts
problem: Code-generating LLMs produce visual artifacts with defects like overlapping elements and clipped text because they commit to code before observing the rendered output.
key_idea: Treat rendered visual feedback as privileged context for a teacher model and distill it into a coding student, with spatially targeted supervision via Visual-Grounded Code Credit Weighting.
method: Visual-SDPO uses self-distillation policy optimization with a weight-sharing teacher that receives visual feedback, a token-level distillation loss weighted by code credit, and a sequence-level GRPO term for executable rollouts.
dataset_or_scenario: ChartMimic, Design2Code, and AeSlides benchmarks for chart, web/UI, and slide generation.
metrics: Primary metric (not named in abstract), pass@k or similar not specified; improvements reported in absolute points.
results_summary: Visual-SDPO improves over zero-shot base by >10 absolute points and over GRPO by at least 2.4 points, with fewer training steps and no added inference cost.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require rendered visual feedback which could be expensive or unavailable in some settings.

title: OpenRTLSet: A Fully Open-Source Dataset for Large Language Model-based Verilog Module Design
problem: The lack of large, fully open-source datasets for Verilog code generation hinders research and commercial use of LLMs in hardware design.
key_idea: Creating the largest fully open-source Verilog dataset by combining code from GitHub, VHDL translations, and C/C++ translations, with paired natural language descriptions generated by DeepSeek-R1.
method: Curated 131k Verilog samples from three sources (GitHub, VHDL translations, C/C++ translations), used DeepSeek-R1 to generate natural language descriptions, and fine-tuned Qwen and Granite models with options like Verilator context, quantization (INT4 vs BF16), and model sizes (7B-32B).
dataset_or_scenario: OpenRTLSet dataset with 131k Verilog modules; fine-tuning on Qwen and Granite model families.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Open-source approaches with OpenRTLSet achieve superior performance in hardware design tasks, establishing a new foundation for accessible research and commercial use.

title: FASE: Fast Adaptive Semantic Entropy for Code Quality
problem: Multi-agent code generation suffers from LLM hallucinations and error propagation, and current semantic entropy methods rely on costly LLM-driven equivalence checks.
key_idea: FASE approximates functional correctness using a minimum spanning tree of structural and semantic dissimilarity graphs, eliminating the need for LLM-driven equivalence evaluation.
method: FASE computes semantic entropy based on the minimum spanning tree of dissimilarity graphs derived from code embeddings, using structural and semantic features.
dataset_or_scenario: HumanEval and BigCodeBench
metrics: Spearman correlation, ROCAUC score, Pass@1 from ground-truth test cases, runtime cost
results_summary: FASE achieves a 25% improvement in Spearman correlation and a 19% increase in ROCAUC over state-of-the-art semantic entropy, while requiring only 0.3% of the runtime cost.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may rely on embedding quality and graph construction assumptions.

title: Code Is More Than Text: Uncertainty Estimation for Code Generation
problem: Existing uncertainty estimation methods for code generation are inherited from natural language generation and ignore properties unique to code, such as token fragility, intent-code gap, and executability.
key_idea: Code differs from natural language in three ways: token fragility, intent-code gap, and executability, which motivate three orthogonal uncertainty axes: lexical, algorithmic, and functional.
method: Proposes a three-axis ensemble for uncertainty estimation: lexical (Top-K token entropy), algorithmic (pseudo-code consistency), and functional (behavioral consistency).
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: AUROC
results_summary: The three-axis ensemble improves average AUROC from 0.696 (strongest NL-derived baseline) to 0.776 (+8.1 points) across five code LLMs. On Qwen3-14B, single-pass Top-K token entropy matches the strongest multi-pass baseline while being over 3x cheaper.

title: PriFT: Prior-Support Guided Supervised Fine-Tuning
problem: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can show weaker generalization than reinforcement learning (RL) due to its off-policy objective that fits fixed demonstrations token by token, including targets poorly aligned with the model's pretrained distribution, leading to overfitting.
key_idea: Deriving token weights from a frozen pretrained reference to obtain a stable reweighting signal unaffected by fine-tuning, estimating prior support for each target token.
method: PriFT computes token weights from a frozen pretrained model instead of the online fine-tuned model, using either token probability (PriFT-prob) or cumulative probability mass (PriFT-mass) to reweight tokens during SFT.
dataset_or_scenario: Mathematical reasoning, code generation, and medical question answering.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract.
results_summary: PriFT achieves state-of-the-art results among SFT baselines and provides a better initialization for subsequent RL training across multiple token-reweighting rules.

title: Multi-task LLMs for Bug Classification: Efficient Inference with Auxiliary Decoding Heads
problem: Existing bug localization techniques are either prohibitively expensive (requiring minutes of agentic reasoning) or operate at coarse function-level granularity, while lightweight line-level methods are limited in performance or context size.
key_idea: A lightweight multi-task LLM with auxiliary decoding heads for efficient line-level bug classification, requiring only a single generated token per file.
method: Introduces a token alignment algorithm to overcome tokenization challenges, a multi-task LLM (MLC) for bug localization, and an optimized training recipe for multi-line prediction.
dataset_or_scenario: Defects4J and PypiBugs benchmarks, plus a small out-of-domain evaluation dataset in Python.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (likely precision/recall/F1 or similar bug localization metrics).
results_summary: Achieves state-of-the-art performance among similar setups on line-level bug localization with full-file context, and comparable performance to agentic approaches while reducing inference latency by orders of magnitude.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may have limited evaluation on out-of-domain datasets (only small Python dataset).

title: LongRTL: Graph-Similarity-Guided LLM-driven Long Context RTL Optimization
problem: Real-world RTL designs are typically long, entangled, and poorly modularized, posing challenges due to context-length limitations and lack of structure for LLM-based optimization.
key_idea: A scalable LLM-based RTL optimization framework guided by graph similarity, using three collaborative agents to decompose, optimize, and reconstruct long RTL designs.
method: The framework uses a Partition Agent to decompose RTL into AST subtrees guided by graph similarity to templates, an Optimization Agent with multi-modal RAG (AST and RTL guidance), and a Reconstruction Agent with logic-aware ordering and Graph-RAG prompting.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Not specified in the abstract

title: Beyond Pass Rate: A Multilingual, Execution-Grounded Evaluation of Open Code LLMs
problem: Current code generation evaluations rely on compact benchmarks and aggregate pass rates, which obscure performance variations across programming languages, problem families, and failure modes.
key_idea: A large-scale, execution-grounded evaluation across 12 programming languages and 9 open LLMs, preserving execution outcomes and static-analysis signals to reveal tradeoffs hidden by single-language or single-metric leaderboards.
method: Evaluated 9 open LLMs on 2,707 LeetCode problems across 12 languages, totaling 325,343 problem-model-language jobs, with each job linked to prompt metadata, extracted code, LeetCode execution outcomes, and static-analysis signals.
dataset_or_scenario: 2,707 free LeetCode problems across 12 programming languages.
metrics: Mean correctness, human acceptance baseline, lint pass rate, compile error rate.
results_summary: Best model Yi-Coder-9B-Chat achieves 23.64% mean correctness vs. 57.2% human baseline; compile errors account for 63.25% of non-accepted submissions; rankings vary by difficulty and language.

title: Lost in the Flow with Code Talkers: Unveiling the Instruction-Tuning Tax of Large Language Models in Code Tasks
problem: The research problem is understanding how instruction tuning affects the feasibility of CodeLLMs as coding assistants, specifically whether the same instruction-tuned paradigm is equally suitable for different code-related tasks.
key_idea: The core novelty is the discovery of an 'Instruction-Tuning Tax', a trade-off where instruction-tuned models gain instruction-following ability but lose infilling performance.
method: The study conducts an empirical analysis comparing instruction-tuned and non-instruction-tuned models on code tasks, using manual failure categorization, behavioral metrics for generation fidelity, and intermediate-checkpoint evaluation throughout tuning.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Behavioral metrics that capture generation fidelity, and intermediate-checkpoint evaluation.
results_summary: Instruction tuning improves instruction-following and structured guidance use but weakens infilling performance, summarized into seven findings and four implications.

title: When LLMs Invent Rust Crates: An Empirical Study of Hallucination Patterns and Mitigation
problem: Large Language Models (LLMs) hallucinate non-existent dependencies (package hallucination) in generated code, posing security risks to the software supply chain, but this phenomenon has not been studied for the Rust language.
key_idea: First large-scale empirical study on crate hallucination in LLM-generated Rust code, revealing distinct hallucination patterns compared to Python and JavaScript, with consistent rates across models and minimal sensitivity to parameters.
method: Constructed a multi-source dataset from Stack Overflow, GitHub, and LLM-generated tasks, and evaluated commercial and open-source models under various decoding settings, then investigated prompt engineering strategies for mitigation.
dataset_or_scenario: Multi-source dataset combining coding tasks from Stack Overflow, GitHub, and LLM-generated tasks.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Hallucination behavior in Rust follows a distinct pattern: different models exhibit surprisingly consistent hallucination rates with minimal sensitivity to model parameters, unlike prior findings in Python and JavaScript.

title: AsyncLane: Decoupling Refinement from Advancement in Diffusion Language Model Decoding
problem: Block-wise semi-autoregressive decoding in diffusion large language models imposes strict dependency between blocks, causing inefficiency as continuation generation must wait for full refinement of the current block.
key_idea: Decouple refinement from advancement by forking a generate lane at delimiter boundaries, allowing continuation to proceed before prefix refinement finishes.
method: AsyncLane is a training-free decoding scheduler that uses lane forking, shared-prefix lane batching, lookahead draft reuse, cascading termination, and compact cache refresh with refresh-logit reuse to enable efficient asynchronous decoding under bidirectional attention.
dataset_or_scenario: Mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks.
metrics: Throughput (TPS) and quality (competitive quality).
results_summary: AsyncLane achieves the highest TPS in all evaluated benchmark-length settings, with peak speedups of 2.95x on LLaDA and 3.04x on Dream relative to the fastest competing baseline, especially under longer generation budgets.

title: Self-Evolving Scientific Agent Discovers Generalizable Physically-Reasoned Fluid Control
problem: The research addresses the challenge of automating controller construction for physical systems while preserving interpretability and physical reasoning, as opposed to black-box deep reinforcement learning.
key_idea: A self-evolving scientific-agent workflow driven by LLMs and iterative code generation that autonomously discovers and refines control policies through simulation-based diagnosis and source-code modifications.
method: The agent deploys candidate strategies into physical simulations, diagnoses dynamic behaviors from multimodal evidence, and translates observations into progressive source-code refinements, iteratively improving the controller.
dataset_or_scenario: A highly non-linear fluid-structure interaction problem: an underactuated two-joint dogfish swimmer tasked with spatial target reaching using only joint angular accelerations.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (implicitly success in target reaching and generalization).
results_summary: The agent autonomously discovers a unified controller that robustly captures all canonical targets and generalizes to unseen static targets and dynamically curved pursuit trajectories without retraining.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may be limited to the specific fluid control scenario and require further validation on diverse physical systems.

title: Smaller Models, Unexpected Costs: Trade-offs in LLM Quantization for Automated Program Repair
problem: The impact of LLM quantization on complex software engineering tasks like Automated Program Repair (APR) is not well understood, as prior work focuses only on benchmark scores and ignores changes in model behavior and non-functional overheads.
key_idea: Quantization reduces memory footprint but can lead to different sets of repaired problems with little overlap, and increases inference time and energy consumption due to suboptimal hardware utilization.
method: Empirical evaluation of 13 quantization configurations (varying bit-widths, methods, and target components) across six LLMs on two APR benchmarks (HumanEval-Java and Defects4J).
dataset_or_scenario: HumanEval-Java and Defects4J benchmarks for Automated Program Repair.
metrics: Number of repaired problems, memory footprint reduction (up to 85%), inference time, energy consumption, Pareto trade-off analysis.
results_summary: Quantized models repair different problems than base models with comparable counts, but increase inference time and energy; 48% of configurations are strictly dominated in Pareto analysis.
limitations: The study is limited to specific LLMs and APR benchmarks; findings may not generalize to other tasks or quantization methods.

title: Welterweight Go: Boxing, Structural Subtyping, and Generics (Extended Version)
problem: Formalizing Go's combination of structural subtyping, generics, and non-uniform runtime representations is challenging, and prior models exclude key features like underlying types, type unions, and generic methods.
key_idea: Introduces WG, a core model capturing Go's key features, and LWG, a lower-level language modeling runtime mechanisms, with a type-directed compilation strategy using runtime type conversions and adaptor methods instead of static monomorphisation.
method: Defines WG (Welterweight Go) as a core calculus and LWG as a runtime model, then provides a type-directed compilation from WG to LWG that handles structural subtyping and generics via runtime type conversions and adaptor methods.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Not specified in the abstract

title: To Run or Not to Run: Analyzing the Cost-Effectiveness of Code Execution in LLM-Based Program Repair
problem: The impact of code execution on LLM-based program repair agents is underexplored, and executions can be time-consuming and expensive.
key_idea: Execution should be treated as a resource with an explicit cost-benefit tradeoff, not a default capability, as its benefit is concentrated and restrictions have little effect on repair success.
method: Two-stage empirical study: first analyzing 7,745 agent traces from SWE-bench leaderboard submissions, then evaluating 3,000 end-to-end repair attempts across 200 SWE-bench instances and three agents under four execution paradigms.
dataset_or_scenario: SWE-bench leaderboard submissions and 200 SWE-bench instances with three agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode).
metrics: Number of test runs per task, resolve-rate gap, token and wall-clock cost.
results_summary: Execution is used across all agents with an average of 8.8 test runs per task; prohibiting execution saves substantial cost with only a 1.25 percentage point resolve-rate gap (not statistically significant).

title: HyperDFlash: MHC-Aligned Block Speculative Decoding with Gated Residual Reduction
problem: The native Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) module in DeepSeek-V4 suffers from draft accuracy degradation at later positions due to error accumulation, and existing DFlash method cannot be adapted to the multi-hyper-connection (MHC) architecture due to feature misalignment.
key_idea: Proposes model-aligned optimizations for MHC residual streams, including pre-collapse residual states as conditioning signal and a lightweight gated residual reducer inherited from the hyper-connection head, along with targeted KL distillation loss.
method: HyperDFlash uses pre-collapse residual states for conditioning, replaces the linear compressor with a gated residual reducer (three orders of magnitude fewer parameters), and enhances training with KL distillation loss on the LM-head.
dataset_or_scenario: Math reasoning, code synthesis, and conversational benchmarks.
metrics: Average accepted draft length and decoding speedup.
results_summary: HyperDFlash consistently outperforms native MTP baseline and vanilla DFlash adaptation, achieving substantial gains in average accepted draft length and decoding speedup.

title: NebulaExp-8B: An Empirical Post-Training Pipeline via Full-Scale Ablation Research
problem: Post-training alignment for large language models lacks transparency in data construction, filtering rules, and training recipes, hindering reproducibility and lightweight model optimization.
key_idea: A fully transparent, ablation-driven post-training pipeline with detailed data processing and training recipes, covering both general instruct and complex reasoning model branches.
method: The pipeline includes a 3.84M SFT corpus and 200K RL candidate pool with end-to-end data processing (distillation, cross-verification filtering, difficulty grading, task classification, diversity sampling). For Instruct branch, three-stage SFT and GRPO RL are used; for Reasoning branch, medium-difficulty GRPO RL. Also investigates OPD (single/multi-teacher) as an alternative to RL.
dataset_or_scenario: Multi-source SFT samples (3.84M) and verifiable RL candidate pool (200K); evaluation on benchmarks including IFEval, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and general knowledge.
metrics: Average benchmark scores; specific gains reported (e.g., Instruct branch from 55.01 to 60.99 after SFT, to 61.85 after RL; Reasoning branch from 73.88 to 75.17; OPD outperforms RL baseline by 3.26 on IFEval with +4.43 average overall gain; MOPD lifts average by 4.18).
results_summary: The NebulaExp pipeline significantly improves performance over the Qwen3-8B-base baseline across both instruct and reasoning branches, with OPD methods showing competitive or superior results to RL while using fewer samples.
limitations: The pipeline is demonstrated only on 8B-scale models; generalizability to other scales or architectures is not explored.

title: Can Large Language Models Reliably Code Qualitative Humanitarian Data? A Benchmark Study Against Human Expert Adjudication
problem: Humanitarian organizations lack the staff and expertise to analyze qualitative data from affected populations at scale, and the reliability of LLMs for coding such data has not been established.
key_idea: A benchmark study comparing 46 LLMs to human experts using synthetic humanitarian transcripts, evaluating reliability with Krippendorff's alpha and qualitative criteria.
method: The study uses 150 high-fidelity synthetic humanitarian transcripts, compares 46 LLMs to a human Gold Standard, and evaluates using inter-rater reliability (Krippendorff's alpha), discrepancy analysis, and qualitative assessment across humanitarian-specific criteria.
dataset_or_scenario: 150 high-fidelity synthetic humanitarian transcripts.
metrics: Krippendorff's alpha, discrepancy analysis (correct, near-correct, incorrect codes), and qualitative assessment across criteria including discrimination, complex needs hierarchies, and non-standard communication styles.
results_summary: Multiple LLMs achieved reliability comparable to experienced human coders, especially with structured prompts and reasoning-enabled configurations, but aggregate metrics alone are insufficient; models varied in recognizing indirect needs and protection concerns.
limitations: The study uses synthetic transcripts, which may not fully capture real-world humanitarian data complexity; findings may not generalize to all humanitarian contexts.

title: Optimizing CUDA like a Human: Micro-Profiling Tools as Expert Surrogates for LLM-Based GPU Kernel Optimization
problem: Automated GPU kernel optimization using LLMs is limited by lack of expert-level profiling feedback and effective search strategies.
key_idea: Integrate pluggable micro-profiling tools that encode expert heuristics as semantic feedback, and use a domain-adapted MCTS for iterative optimization.
method: KernelPro is a closed-loop multi-agent system with semantic feedback operator, two-stage tool invocation architecture, domain-adapted MCTS with progressive widening and search memory, and direct CuTe source-level code generation via autonomous code search.
dataset_or_scenario: KernelBench (Levels 1/2/3) and VeOmni's expert-optimized MoE training kernels.
metrics: Geometric mean speedups, energy reduction percentage, p-values for ablation studies.
results_summary: KernelPro achieves geometric mean speedups of 2.42x/4.69x/5.30x on KernelBench Levels 1/2/3, and 1.23x over hand-tuned Triton on MoE kernels, with 11.6% energy reduction at matched speed.

title: Axon: A Synthesizing Superoptimizer for Tensor Programs
problem: Writing high-performance kernels for AI accelerators requires deep expertise in tiling, instruction selection, data layout, and operator fusion, placing a significant burden on programmers.
key_idea: Axon uses program synthesis to automatically generate target instructions from semantics specifications and explores semantically equivalent program variants to select the best performing kernel empirically.
method: Axon discovers algebraic transformations by propagating operators through computation graphs and uses SMT over unbounded tensors to guarantee semantics preservation. It lowers tensor operations to target ISA instructions, explores tiling configurations constrained by hardware descriptions, and fuses operators and instructions to minimize memory traffic.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Not specified in the abstract

title: Weave of Formal Thought
problem: Large language models for code lack formal guarantees of syntactic validity and do not leverage hierarchical structure of target languages, while existing constrained-decoding methods are incomplete and code LLMs inject grammar via predetermined policies rather than learning.
key_idea: Uniting rigorous syntactic validation via a sound and complete constrained decoder with learned structural representations through latent-variable fine-tuning that interleaves non-terminal grammar symbols.
method: Proposes a formal engine and constrained decoder using speculative-lexing with GLR parsing for sound and complete validation against Tree-sitter; introduces latent-variable fine-tuning with reweighted wake-sleep algorithm to optimize IW-ELBO, training the model to interleave grammar symbols.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Per-token cross-entropy reduction relative to text-only SFT baseline.
results_summary: Fine-tuning StarCoder2-3B with the RWS objective reduces per-token cross-entropy by 14.3% relative to a text-only SFT baseline, showing that latent syntax recovers structural information.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include computational overhead of the constrained decoder and applicability to languages beyond Python.

title: AI-Assisted Computational Reproducibility on the FABRIC Testbed
problem: Computational reproducibility remains difficult despite being central to scientific research.
key_idea: Combining the FABRIC testbed with LLM coding assistants (LoomAI) to simplify reproducing published experiments across multiple domains.
method: Reproduced three case studies (BBR congestion control, LAMMPS molecular dynamics, stress protein genomics) using AI assistant for environment setup, code adaptation, and debugging, with human guidance for analysis stages.
dataset_or_scenario: Three case studies: BBR-family congestion-control evaluations, LAMMPS molecular dynamics scaling benchmarks on CPU-only MPI cluster, stress protein homeostasis genomics pipelines.
metrics: Reduction in reproduction effort (roughly 4-6 times).
results_summary: AI-assisted workflow reduced reproduction effort by roughly 4-6 times across case studies, but struggled with analysis stages lacking defined workflows.
limitations: AI assistant struggled with analysis stages lacking clearly defined workflows, requiring human guidance for execution order and data dependencies.

title: OPERA: Aligning Open-Ended Reasoning via Objective Perplexity-based Reinforcement Learning
problem: Applying reinforcement learning to open-ended tasks like creative writing is challenging because LLM-as-a-judge reward models exhibit stylistic biases and positional inconsistencies, leading to unstable supervision.
key_idea: Replace unreliable external judges with intrinsic rewards derived from perplexity dynamics, quantifying uncertainty reduction at critical reflective states.
method: Proposes OPERA, which uses perplexity dynamics as intrinsic reward signal, a cold-start data synthesis method with guiding words and perplexity-prioritized rollouts to generate diverse reasoning traces, resulting in a 20,000 trajectory dataset.
dataset_or_scenario: A large-scale dataset of 20,000 high-quality reasoning trajectories for open-ended tasks.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract.
results_summary: OPERA on Qwen3-8B establishes a new state-of-the-art among open-source models, achieving parity with or surpassing proprietary models like Gemini2.5 and MiniMax-M2.5 in some open-ended tasks.

title: CodeChat-Eval: Evaluating Large Language Models in Multi-Turn Code Refinement Dialogues
problem: Existing benchmarks evaluate LLMs on single-turn code generation, but cannot assess whether LLMs maintain functional correctness during multi-turn code refinement dialogues where developers provide follow-up instructions.
key_idea: Introduces CodeChat-Eval, an evaluation framework that constructs evaluation sessions from multi-turn code refinement dialogues using a dynamic instruction selection algorithm.
method: CodeChat-Eval uses a dynamic instruction selection algorithm to build evaluation sessions from multi-turn dialogues, then measures functional correctness of refined code against original test suites.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Functional correctness (whether refined code passes the test suite for the original task).
results_summary: Empirical study on open-weight and proprietary LLMs shows a statistically significant decrease in functional correctness over multi-turn refinement, ranging from 19.2% (GPT-5 Nano) to 69.2% (Llama 3.1 8B), with largest drops for logic-level refinements and additive changes.

title: AlgoEvolve: LLM-driven Meta-evolution of Algorithmic Trading Programs
problem: Extending LLM-driven evolutionary program synthesis from static coding benchmarks to the challenging domain of algorithmic trading, which is noisy, non-stationary, and highly discontinuous.
key_idea: Using LLMs as semantic mutation operators in an evolutionary framework with a meta-evolutionary outer loop that evolves prompts to improve search heuristics for program synthesis.
method: AlgoEvolve generates, evaluates, and iteratively improves executable trading strategies expressed as Python code via LLM-driven evolution, with a meta-evolutionary outer loop that evolves prompts guiding the inner loop synthesis.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract; algorithmic trading domain with multiple experiments.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract; mentions zero-trade failures and outperformance of human-designed instructions.
results_summary: The system exhibits emergent regime-adaptive strategy logic and the meta-evolutionary outer loop discovers improved search heuristics that balance exploration and exploitation, reducing zero-trade failures and consistently outperforming initial human-designed instructions.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on LLM quality and computational cost of meta-evolution.

title: Quantization Inflates Reasoning: Token Inflation as a Hidden Cost of Low-Bit Reasoning Models
problem: Quantization of large language models for reasoning tasks can increase reasoning-token usage (token inflation) even when accuracy is preserved, offsetting expected speedups and introducing hidden costs.
key_idea: Introduces the CoT Token Inflation Ratio to measure the increase in reasoning length in quantized models and identifies behavioral changes like more intermediate steps and semantic repetition.
method: Evaluates INT4/INT3 post-training quantization on reasoning models across multiple benchmarks, measures token inflation ratio, and tests mitigation strategies including prompting, decoding-time sampling, and quantization-aware training.
dataset_or_scenario: Mathematical reasoning, code generation, scientific question answering, and agentic tool-use benchmarks.
metrics: CoT Token Inflation Ratio, accuracy, per-token latency, end-to-end serving penalties.
results_summary: INT4/INT3 quantization preserves accuracy but increases reasoning-token usage, leading to token inflation. Quantization-aware training shows promise in reducing both accuracy degradation and token inflation, while prompting and sampling offer inconsistent trade-offs.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; mitigation strategies like prompting and decoding-time sampling show inconsistent trade-offs.

title: LibEvoBench: Probing Temporal Knowledge Stratification in Code Generation Models
problem: Large software projects depend on older library versions, but LLMs lack mechanisms for version-specific reasoning, causing anachronistic errors when calling APIs from different versions.
key_idea: Introduces LibEvoBench, a multi-task benchmark spanning multiple versions of Python libraries, and the Software Evolution Understanding Score (SEUS) to measure consistency with evolving APIs.
method: Constructs a benchmark with tasks across library versions and evaluates models on version-specific API usage, comparing performance with and without version specification or documentation.
dataset_or_scenario: LibEvoBench, covering multiple versions of widely used Python libraries.
metrics: Software Evolution Understanding Score (SEUS), performance degradation for evolving APIs vs. stable APIs.
results_summary: State-of-the-art models are largely version-oblivious; specifying the target version provides no benefit, but relevant documentation significantly boosts accuracy.

title: SoK: AI Secure Code Generation: Progress, Pitfalls, and Paths Forward
problem: The field lacks a systematic understanding of how techniques like prompting, fine-tuning, and agentic workflows improve secure code generation and why substantial failures persist.
key_idea: Introduces a three-level framework measuring natural-language understanding of secure coding principles, code-level actuation, and the knowledge-actuation gaps between them.
method: Proposes a framework instantiated across models and coding agents on benchmarks covering function-level and web-application security, analyzing the relationship between principle understanding and code outcomes.
dataset_or_scenario: Benchmarks covering isolated function-level security and full web-application security.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (implied: functional correctness, security, joint functional-security correctness).
results_summary: Secure-coding-principle understanding is a strong predictor of code-level outcomes, but substantial knowledge-actuation gaps remain where models recognize principles yet fail to produce secure and functional code.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; inferred: the framework may not cover all security aspects or model types.

title: LLM4MTLs: Automated Generation and Empirical Evaluation of Model Transformation Languages
problem: Developing correct model transformations using LLMs is challenging due to limited training data and executable examples, resulting in syntactically invalid or semantically unusable code.
key_idea: An automated workflow for constructing and comparing prompting strategies for LLM-generated MTL code, combined with an evaluation suite and empirical evaluation.
method: Systematically explores prompt constructions combining few-shot prompting, grammar prompting, and helper method inclusion, evaluated across three LLMs and four MTLs using syntactic and semantic metrics.
dataset_or_scenario: Evaluation suite spanning four MTLs (ATL, ETL, QVTo, and the Reactions language) with executable reference scripts and manually written test suites.
metrics: Syntactic and semantic metrics, including Pass@1 for semantic correctness.
results_summary: Few-shot prompting consistently improves syntactic quality across all MTLs but gains in semantic correctness are uneven and language-dependent; grammar prompting stabilizes generation with few-shot examples but can be counterproductive alone.
limitations: Semantic correctness improvements are limited and language-dependent; LLM choice has limited influence on semantic correctness.

title: Dream at SemEval-2026 Task 13: SALSA for Single-Pass Machine-Generated Code Detection
problem: Detecting machine-generated code to address concerns about authorship, assessment integrity, and software trust, with a focus on out-of-distribution generalization across unseen programming languages and domains.
key_idea: A SALSA-style formulation (Single-pass Autoregressive LLM Structured Classification) that maps each class to a dedicated output token and trains the model to emit a single-token label in a structured response, delegating authorship decisions to the model.
method: Combines balanced sampling across languages with parameter-efficient fine-tuning and conservative training (low learning rate, single epoch) to avoid overfitting, using a single-pass autoregressive LLM for binary classification.
dataset_or_scenario: SemEval-2026 Task 13 Subtask A, with emphasis on out-of-distribution generalization across unseen programming languages and application domains.
metrics: F1 score (OOD F1 = 0.789 on official leaderboard).
results_summary: The best system achieves OOD F1 = 0.789, substantially outperforming the CodeBERT baseline (F1 = 0.305).
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; potential limitations include reliance on a single autoregressive model and possible sensitivity to hyperparameter choices.

title: ReNIO: Reweighting Negative Trajectory Importance for LLM On-Policy Distillation
problem: Standard on-policy distillation treats all student-generated outputs equally, ignoring the varying informativeness of correct and incorrect trajectories for improving LLM reasoning.
key_idea: Incorrect student-generated outputs are more informative than correct ones for preserving exploratory reasoning near the model's capability boundary, and this signal can be exploited without requiring full answer correctness.
method: ReNIO reweights negative trajectories by using the student-to-teacher probability ratio to identify pivotal tokens leading to wrong reasoning traces, aggregating them into a normalized sample weight that assigns larger weights to likely negative trajectories without observing final-answer correctness.
dataset_or_scenario: Mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks.
metrics: Relative gains (e.g., up to 8.90% for Qwen3-1.7B and 10.00% for R1-Distill-Qwen-7B on mathematical reasoning benchmarks).
results_summary: ReNIO improves both OPD and OPSD across mathematical reasoning and code generation, achieving up to 8.90% and 10.00% relative gains on mathematical reasoning benchmarks for two model sizes.

title: AI Scientists as Engines of Discovery: A Case for Development within Reformed Institutions
problem: The paper addresses the qualitative transition of AI from passive computational tools to active 'AI scientists' that can expand hypothesis generation and verification in scientific discovery, and the need for institutional redesign to accommodate this shift.
key_idea: Multi-agent AI systems, illustrated by the prototype framework Denario, can accelerate the discovery cycle and explore model spaces beyond human reach, necessitating reformed institutions for verification, accountability, interpretability, and dual-use safety.
method: The paper sketches multi-agent architectures and uses the prototype framework Denario to illustrate how such systems accelerate the discovery cycle and traverse model spaces beyond human reach.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Not specified in the abstract

title: Finding the Evidence: Discovering Decision-Supporting Tokens for On-Policy Reasoning Distillation
problem: On-policy distillation for reasoning tasks fails to transfer substantive knowledge from evidence tokens in reasoning chains, capturing only decision tokens.
key_idea: Reasoning chains contain two types of knowledge—decisions and evidence—requiring different discovery mechanisms; evidence tokens are identified via hidden-state similarity and teacher-student divergence.
method: DEAR identifies decision tokens via student entropy, then discovers supporting evidence tokens using hidden-state cosine similarity to decision anchors, boosted by teacher-student divergence to prioritize knowledge gaps.
dataset_or_scenario: Math and code benchmarks across three student-teacher configurations.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (results reported in percentage points improvement).
results_summary: DEAR consistently outperforms standard OPD, with up to +2.5pp on competition math and +5.7pp on code generation.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may require careful tuning of similarity and divergence thresholds.

title: Text2DSL: LLM-Based Code Generation for Domain-Specific Languages
problem: Manually authoring DSL rules for OS security policies is error-prone and requires high expertise; existing code generation approaches do not address DSL-specific challenges.
key_idea: Formalizing Text2DSL as a distinct problem class and demonstrating that injecting structured context (BNF grammar, API spec, identifier vocabulary) into prompts is a robust enabling factor for high-quality DSL code generation without fine-tuning.
method: Introduced PolkitBench dataset with 4,204 verified NL-to-Polkit-rule pairs validated via three-level AST pipeline; conducted controlled prompt experiments on two MoE models (GigaChat-10B-A1.8B and Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B) comparing with and without structured context.
dataset_or_scenario: PolkitBench dataset (4,204 NL-to-Polkit-rule pairs) for OS security policy DSL generation.
metrics: Syntactic validity, structural validity, CodeBLEU score.
results_summary: Supplying context raised syntactic validity to 98.6-99.4%, structural validity by +9.7 to +35.5 pp, and CodeBLEU by +60% to +95% across both models.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may include limited domain (Polkit rules) and reliance on specific prompt engineering.

title: Formal-Method-Guided Vibe Coding: Closing the Verification Loop on AI-Generated Safety-Critical Software Through Model-Driven Engineering
problem: LLM-generated code lacks formal correctness guarantees, making it unsuitable for safety-critical systems that require certification under standards like DO-178C, IEC 61508, or ISO 26262.
key_idea: A closed-loop pipeline that uses Model-Driven Engineering to extract formal artefacts from LLM-generated Java code and applies multiple verifiers, feeding verification failures back as structured prompts to iteratively improve the code.
method: Forge pipeline: generate Java code via vibe coding, extract formal models (Dafny, CSP, Z-Machines) through model transformations, verify them with complementary verifiers (Dafny, FDR4, Isabelle), and use failures to create correction prompts for the next iteration.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: The pipeline produces standards-relevant verification evidence for LLM-generated Java, representing a step toward certification of AI-generated safety-critical software.

title: TraceView: Interactive Visualization of Agentic Program Repair Trajectories
problem: LLM-based automated program repair agents produce long trajectories that are difficult to diagnose when repairs fail, as final outcomes do not reveal how the agent reached that outcome or where the process became repetitive or misaligned.
key_idea: TraceView provides an interactive tool for labeling and visualizing repair trajectories with Thought, Action, and Result components, enabling semantic relation labeling and diagnosis through graph views and filters.
method: TraceView organizes raw and pre-labeled agentic runs into components, renders trajectories as graph views, and provides relation filters, patch outcome summaries, metrics, and node-level evidence panels for inspection.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: In a survey-based user study with five researchers, participants reported that TraceView made trajectories easier to scan and its overview-to-detail workflow helped them better understand repair behavior.
limitations: The evaluation is limited to five researchers in a survey-based study, and the abstract does not discuss scalability or generalizability to other APR systems.

title: CodeTeam: An LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Framework for Repository-Level Code Generation
problem: Natural language to repository generation (NL2Repo) requires constructing an entire software repository from a natural-language requirements document, which demands longer planning horizons, stable interfaces across files, and iterative debugging of cross-file inconsistencies.
key_idea: CodeTeam separates planning, decision making, and implementation into distinct, coordinated stages using multiple LLM-based agents, including Architect agents for design sketches, a CTO agent for evaluation and normalization, Developer agents for dependency-aware code generation, and a QA agent for testing and repair.
method: CodeTeam uses a multi-agent framework with a planning stage where multiple Architect agents draft software design sketches (SDS) optionally grounded by retrieved design references, a CTO agent evaluates and normalizes the best SDS into a machine-checkable contract, and an implementation stage with Developer agents under a dependency-aware scheduler and Git-based coordination, plus a QA agent for testing and iterative repairs.
dataset_or_scenario: SketchEval benchmark (synthesis-based) and NL2Repo-Bench benchmark (execution-based).
metrics: SketchBLEU, average test pass rate.
results_summary: CodeTeam improves SketchBLEU by 4.1 and 2.9 absolute points over CodeS variants in prompt-engineering and supervised fine-tuning settings, respectively, and achieves the highest average test pass rate on NL2Repo-Bench (34.6% PE, 42.3% SFT).

title: A11YRepair: Bridging Web Accessibility Barriers via Knowledge-Enhanced Divide-and-Conquer Repair
problem: Existing tools focus on detecting web accessibility violations but fail to repair them, and current automated program repair techniques perform poorly on real-world A11Y issues due to multi-fault, multi-file nature.
key_idea: A divide-and-conquer workflow that clusters related violations and decomposes them by root cause, combined with WCAG-driven knowledge for domain-aware fault localization and patch synthesis.
method: A11YRepair uses an LLM-based framework with a divide-and-conquer approach: first clustering violations requiring coordinated edits, then decomposing each cluster by root cause for focused patch generation, incorporating WCAG knowledge.
dataset_or_scenario: A11YBench, a benchmark of 60 real-world web projects collected from GitHub.
metrics: Repair effectiveness and cost (not specified in detail).
results_summary: A11YRepair achieves higher repair effectiveness and lower cost than state-of-the-art baselines; patches have been merged into open-source projects from major companies.

title: AgentDSE: Reasoning-Augmented Architectural Design Space Exploration
problem: Traditional architectural design space exploration (DSE) is inefficient, requiring tens of thousands of simulator evaluations because conventional methods treat the simulator as a black-box oracle.
key_idea: AgentDSE uses a general-purpose LLM coding agent to automate the architectural-reasoning loop, mimicking human architects who reason through physical constraints and performance bottlenecks.
method: AgentDSE is a simulator-in-the-loop methodology driven by an LLM coding agent that automates architectural reasoning without fine-tuning, precomputed databases, or domain-specific optimizer code.
dataset_or_scenario: DNN accelerator mapping, hardware/software co-design, and CPU cache-hierarchy optimization.
metrics: Design quality and number of evaluations (up to two orders of magnitude fewer).
results_summary: AgentDSE achieves competitive or better design quality with up to two orders of magnitude fewer evaluations compared to traditional methods.

title: CNnotator: LLM-Guided Memory Safety Annotation Synthesis
problem: Memory safety errors are prevalent in C code, and migrating to safer languages requires understanding how legacy code manipulates memory, which is only implicitly represented.
key_idea: Using large language models to automatically synthesize CN specifications that represent memory usage patterns, enabling memory safety annotation for C programs.
method: CNnotator uses LLMs to generate CN specifications and then tests them automatically; it evaluates both reasoning and chat models on small-to-medium C programs.
dataset_or_scenario: Small-to-medium C programs (not further specified in the abstract).
metrics: Success rate on first attempts and overall success rate.
results_summary: OpenAI o3 reasoning model achieved 90% success on first attempts and 97% overall, while GPT-4o achieved 65% on first attempts.
limitations: The approach is evaluated only on small-to-medium programs; scalability to large codebases and generalizability to diverse memory patterns are not addressed.

title: The Alignment Problem in Constrained Code Generation
problem: Constrained decoding for code generation can suffer from misalignment between the constrainer, language model, and target language, leading to reduced functional correctness.
key_idea: The incompleteness of constrainers distorts the language model distribution, pushing it into low-probability regions and harming performance.
method: Evaluates constrained decoding with type and syntax enforcements across seven language models and two target languages, studying the impact of varying incompleteness levels.
dataset_or_scenario: Three benchmarks for code generation.
metrics: Functional correctness, timeout rate.
results_summary: Unconstrained decoding significantly outperforms constrained decoding when the constrainer is incomplete, reducing functional correctness by up to 97%.

title: SwarmX: Agentic Scheduling for Low-Latency Agentic Systems
problem: Agentic AI applications composed of multiple model calls and tool executions create scheduling challenges for GPU-CPU clusters due to inference time and model-call structure depending on prompt semantics, making conventional scheduling approaches ineffective for low-latency serving.
key_idea: SwarmX uses scheduling-specific neural predictors to capture prompt, device, runtime, and target-model features, and exposes distributional predictions to routers and scalers for tail-aware decisions.
method: SwarmX integrates neural predictors and mechanisms for training and online adaptation into a scheduler-agent framework that provides a common substrate for integration with existing scheduling and model-serving infrastructure.
dataset_or_scenario: Multi-agent code generation, deep research, and multimodal agentic workflows.
metrics: Tail latency reduction and throughput under SLO.
results_summary: SwarmX reduces tail latency by up to 61.5% compared to state-of-the-art schedulers and sustains up to 2x the throughput of production schedulers under the same SLO.

title: KBSpec: LLM-driven Formal Specification Generation with Evolving Domain Knowledge Base
problem: Large language models struggle to generate syntactically correct and semantically verifiable formal specifications due to the lack of formal specification language corpora.
key_idea: Augment LLMs with dual-source knowledge from official documentation and verifier feedback, maintained in a self-evolving knowledge base without parameter tuning or labeled data.
method: KBSpec maintains a knowledge base that is continuously updated from successful generation and repair trajectories, combining external documentation and internal verifier feedback to guide LLM-based specification generation.
dataset_or_scenario: Java Modeling Language (JML) specification generation evaluated with three LLM backends.
metrics: Verification pass rates and number of high-completeness specifications.
results_summary: KBSpec improves verification pass rates by 10-25% over state-of-the-art LLM-based approaches and produces the largest number of high-completeness specifications.

title: The Substrate Collapse: AI Code Generation Invalidates Authorship-Based Knowledge Metrics
problem: The paper argues that AI code generation severs the inference that authoring code implies understanding, invalidating authorship-based knowledge metrics like truck factor and degree-of-knowledge.
key_idea: AI code generation decouples authorship from comprehension, making authorship-based metrics unreliable for estimating knowledge concentration.
method: The paper presents a theoretical argument and a falsifiable prediction: systems with healthy authorship-derived truck factor but low comprehension-measured retention will suffer incident-resolution failures not predicted by authorship metrics.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: Not specified in the abstract; the paper argues for invalidation of authorship-based metrics and leaves open the problem of building comprehension-grounded instruments.
limitations: The paper does not provide empirical validation or a concrete replacement metric; it leaves the open measurement problem for future work.

title: When Do Intrinsic Rewards Work for Code Reasoning? A Comprehensive Study
problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) relies on costly ground-truth supervision, and it is unclear whether intrinsic reward methods that work for math reasoning transfer effectively to code generation, which has distinct challenges.
key_idea: A systematic empirical study of certainty-based intrinsic reward methods (RLIF) for code generation, revealing that they yield early gains but inevitably collapse, and do not improve RLVR pre-training.
method: Extensive experiments on LiveCodeBench evaluating certainty-based RLIF approaches under different training scenarios and hyperparameter settings.
dataset_or_scenario: LiveCodeBench
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (likely pass@k or similar code generation metrics)
results_summary: Certainty-based methods show early gains but collapse with shortened outputs and lost reasoning; collapse speed depends on sample size and temperature; RLIF pre-training offers no significant improvement over training from scratch.
limitations: The study focuses on certainty-based methods; other intrinsic reward approaches may behave differently. The findings are based on specific hyperparameter settings and may not generalize to all code reasoning tasks.

title: Formally Verified Code Synthesis for Structured Data Translation in a Medical Internet of Things
problem: Ensuring that synthesized code for structured data translation in Medical IoT is trustworthy and reliable.
key_idea: Integrating formal verification into an LLM-powered evolutionary code synthesis pipeline to guarantee generated code satisfies predefined requirements.
method: An LLM-powered evolutionary code synthesis system that includes a formal verification step to ensure generated translation code always maps input JSON to the target FHIR schema.
dataset_or_scenario: Case study integrating a pulse oximeter into an existing network of devices, translating between its JSON schema and FHIR format.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract
results_summary: The system consistently generates correct translations at low cost.

title: Video2Code: Generating Interactive Webpages from UI Videos via Action-Aware Revisit
problem: Existing video-capable vision-language models fail to generate interactive webpages from UI videos because they miss short action boundaries and break state-action-state transitions due to sparse sampling or compressed temporal representations.
key_idea: Instead of uniform visual budget allocation, Video2Code performs coarse video understanding to locate action-critical regions and then revisits them at higher temporal resolution to recover executable UI state transitions.
method: Video2Code first conducts coarse video understanding to identify action-critical regions, then uses a temporal clipping tool to revisit these regions at higher temporal resolution before generating HTML/CSS/JavaScript code, with action-aligned video-code supervision.
dataset_or_scenario: Not specified in the abstract
metrics: Visual and functional criteria, including functional correctness.
results_summary: Video2Code substantially strengthens the underlying open-source model for UI video-to-code generation, improving functional correctness over direct video observation, especially on dense multi-step interactions.
